items.title: Hong Kong: Joshua Wong Gets Nearly 10 More Years in Prison
items.description: Click to expand Image Joshua Wong speaks to protesters near the Legislative Council in Hong Kong, June 17, 2019. © 2019 Kin Cheung/AP Photo (Tokyo) – The Hong Kong High Court on November 5, 2026, sentenced Joshua Wong, a well-known democracy activist, to 10 years in prison on baseless national security charges, Human Rights Watch said today. Two months of the sentence will run concurrently with his current national security sentence. Wong has been in custody since November 2020, when he was 23, and faces imprisonment until late 2036, when he will be 40. The Hong Kong government should immediately and unconditionally release Wong. Foreign governments should denounce the sentences against him and other wrongfully detained pro-democracy activists and impose targeted sanctions on officials responsible for Hong Kong’s growing repression. “The harsh sentence on baseless charges against Joshua Wong is cruel and unjust,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Young people promoting social change are an asset for any vibrant society, but the Hong Kong government puts them behind bars.” To keep Hong Kong society subdued, and to reduce the chance of an international outcry, the Hong Kong government appears to have adopted the tactic of stacking charges against influential pro-democracy leaders to ensure their prolonged detention, Human Rights Watch said. Other notable Hong Kong figures who have faced similar tactics include Jimmy Lai, founder of Apple Daily, and veteran democracy activists Lee Cheuk-yan and Albert Ho. The court sentenced Wong, 30, under the National Security Law for “conspiring to collude with foreign forces.” The authorities accused him of “conspiring” with the activist Nathan Law and other “unknown” individuals between 2016 and November 2020 to urge foreign governments to sanction Hong Kong and Chinese government officials as they advocated for Hong Kong’s “democratic self-determination.” The prosecution relied heavily on the international lobbying and media advocacy that Wong and Demosisto, the political party Wong co-founded in 2016, carried out before the National Security Law took effect. Wong initiated online petitions, spoke to international media, and met with foreign officials to draw attention to human rights abuses in Hong Kong. He urged governments to sanction Chinese and Hong Kong officials responsible for abuses and to stop selling weapons to Hong Kong police that they use to carry out rights violations. Wong had mostly stopped these activities before the National Security Law became effective. Demosisto disbanded on June 30, 2020, and Wong resigned from the group. However, the government quoted social media posts by Wong as ostensible evidence that his alleged “conspiracy” with Law to commit “foreign collusion” continued after the law took effect. In these posts, Wong said he “would not change his views” and that he would “continue to seek support from the international community” in his personal capacity, while Law and others abroad would continue their international advocacy. The government also cited Wong’s subsequent opinion pieces and media interviews, though none directly called for sanctions, which the National Security Law specifically prohibits. It also cited his reposts of Law’s posts broadly calling for sanctions against Chinese officials and Hong Kong police. The court ruled that Wong’s offense was of a “grave nature.” The National Security Law sets prison terms of 3 to 10 years for “foreign collusion,” or 10 years to life for offenses deemed to be of a “grave nature.” Wong formally pleaded guilty on September 2. A guilty plea normally results in a one-third sentence reduction. But a sentence reduction cannot bring the term below the statutory minimum. Because of reporting restrictions on pretrial committal proceedings, when a magistrate determines whether to send a case to a higher court for trial, the public did not know the details of the accusations against Wong until the formal plea. The government enacted a law in 2024 to enable the court, on national security grounds, to deny the defendant’s right to ask the court to lift restrictions on reporting about the case. By restricting media reporting on the pretrial proceedings in national security cases, the government can control the narrative and undermine the fundamental legal principle of open justice. Since Beijing imposed the National Security Law on Hong Kong in June 2020, Hong Kong authorities have used the new legal regime—along with existing laws—to rapidly dismantle civil society and detain, imprison, or force into exile hundreds of activists and government critics. Wong has been in custody since November 2020, when he pleaded guilty to two charges of organizing and inciting an unauthorized assembly linked to the 2019 citywide protest movement. After that, he pleaded guilty to five more charges on separate occasions, including for violating an anti-mask law, participating in an unauthorized vigil for the 1989 Tiananmen Massacre, and breaching a court ban to disclose a police officer’s personal information. While serving these sentences, Wong was charged with two national security offenses, which carry far harsher penalties. In January 2021, Wong was charged with “conspiring to commit subversion” for participating in an unofficial democratic primary in 2020 and sentenced to another four years and eight months in prison. Before Wong could complete these sentences, the authorities brought the “foreign collusion” charge against him in June 2025, ensuring that he would remain in prison. Wong became one of Hong Kong’s best-known democracy activists as a teenager, after leading a massive 2012 protest against a government educational curriculum widely seen as political indoctrination. He became the global face of Hong Kong’s democracy movement during the 2014 Umbrella Movement and co-founded Demosisto with Law and others in 2016. The party disbanded on June 30, 2020, hours before the National Security Law came into effect. The National Security Law’s sweeping provisions have been used to punish peaceful protest and expression. Its use against Wong and others violates the right to freedom of expression under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which is incorporated into Hong Kong law through the city’s de facto constitution, the Basic Law, and the Bill of Rights Ordinance. “Beijing has paid no real price for its increasing repression in Hong Kong,” Pearson said. “Concerned governments should press for the release of Wong and other activists, impose targeted sanctions against implicated officials, and review their relationship with China more broadly in light of the deepening abuses.”

items.title: GNI overhauls claims operations, clears N3bn claims
items.description: By Rosemary Iwunze In a decisive move to reclaim its market position and confidence, Great Nigeria Insurance Plc, GNI, has undertaken a comprehensive overhaul of its claims operations, clearing over N3 billion in claims. According to the company, the liquidation of these liabilities marks one of the most aggressive debt-clearing exercises in the company’s recent history, signaling a clean break from operational bottlenecks. Recognizing that prompt claims settlement remains the primary test of an insurer’s value proposition, GNI’s Executive Management placed its priority on financial restructuring to address long-standing obligations. Having reconstituted its board of Directors and Executive Management, GNI Plc took a bold resolution to confront structural and systemic challenges undermining its operations over the years. At the epicenter of these challenges is the accumulation of outstanding claims that had severely tarnished customer confidence and strained relationships with key industry stakeholders.The organization therefore, placed immediate claims settlement at the core of its corporate turnaround strategy. Meanwhile, GNI hosted two strategic brokers’ fora themed “GNI Reloaded” in Ibadan and Lagos to formalize this operational shift and rebuild crucial trade channels, given that insurance brokers facilitate a significant percentage of commercial and institutional policies in Nigeria. GNI stated: “To prevent future backlogs and ensure long-term operational efficiency, GNI’s Executive Management has instituted a maximum 48-hour Turnaround Time (TAT) window for processing and paying verified claims. Under this new service level agreement (SLA), once a claim is documented and verified by adjusters, payment authorization must occur within 48 hours.” Management emphasizes that this policy is not merely a promotional promise, but an embedded operational mandate backed by streamlined digital workflows and revamped internal approval controls. “By combining substantial capital deployment with structural service delivery reforms, Great Nigeria Insurance Plc aims to position itself as a reliable and responsive player in Nigeria’s evolving financial services sector.” The post GNI overhauls claims operations, clears N3bn claims appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Qui est Abdul El-Sayed, premier sénateur musulman des États-Unis ?
items.description: Une très mauvaise nouvelle pour le président américain, Donald Trump. Le Parti démocrate a repris le contrôle des deux chambres du Congrès, avec en prime la victoire d’Abdul El-Sayed qui a remporté le siège vacant de l’État clé du Michigan au Sénat, à l’issue des élections de mi-mandat qui se sont déroulées mardi 3 novembre. Il devient ainsi le premier sénateur musulman des États-Unis . Pro-palestinien, critique du soutien américain à Israël et figure de l’aile gauche du Parti démocrate, El-Sayed s’est imposé en dépit du retournement de dernière minute opéré par la démocrate Halley Stevens qui a apporté son soutien au candidat républicain, Mike Rogers. Il a obtenu 52,52 % des voix contre 45,48 % pour son rival républicain. D’origine égyptienne, Abdul El Sayed, 42 ans, est docteur en médecine et occupe le poste de directeur de la santé de Détroit depuis 2015. Son entrée au Sénat américain s’inscrit dans le cadre de la montée des idées de gauche aux États-Unis qui a pris forme dans le sillage du succès électoral de Zohran Mamdani à la tête de la mairie de New York. Le désormais premier sénateur musulman des États-Unis a fait l’objet d’une virulente campagne de dénigrement et de harcèlement conduite par le président Trump qui l’a qualifié, entre autres, de « djihadiste ». L’AIPAC, le puissant lobby juif américain, a dépensé des dizaines de millions de dollars pour empêcher son investiture, en vain. Abdul El-Sayed, premier sénateur musulman des États-Unis Donald Trump, pour une fois, n’a pas contesté les résultats de ces élections de mi-mandat (Midterms) qui portent sur le renouvellement total des membres de la Chambre des représentants et le renouvellement d’un tiers des membres du Sénat. Le camp des Démocrates compte désormais 54 sénateurs, dont 7 nouveaux sièges obtenus à l’issue de ce scrutin, contre 44 pour le Parti républicain. Dans la chambre des représentants, les Démocrates ont obtenu 228 sièges contre 139 sièges pour les Républicains. Ces changements dans la composante du Sénat et de la Chambre des représentants constituent un réel frein à la politique du président en exercice, sur les plans législatif et budgétaire. Cela sans compter la possibilité pour le Sénat de déclencher des enquêtes. De nombreux observateurs ont qualifié ce scrutin de « vote sanction », intervenu dans un contexte marqué notamment par une forte baisse du pouvoir d’achat des citoyens américains et en raison de la guerre menée par les États-Unis contre l’Iran. items.title: FDI: Qatar’s Barzan Holdings seeks to deepen defense partnerships with Nigeria
items.description: By Tunde Oso Barzan Holdings, Qatar’s leading national defence and security company, has spotlighted its cutting-edge defence technologies and industrial capabilities at the 2026 Africa International Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX), held in Lagos, as part of efforts to advance defence innovation, strengthen industry collaboration and support Nigeria’s evolving security needs. As one of the sponsors of the exhibition, Barzan Holdings engaged with Nigerian defence stakeholders to explore commercial, technological and industrial collaborations across its four business sectors: weapons and ammunition; advanced technology; platforms; and services, support and accessories. Beyond equipment supply, the company offers capabilities across the defence lifecycle, including training, maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), and technical support. Its portfolio includes unmanned surface vessels and unmanned aerial vehicles for surveillance and intelligence missions, as well as command-and-control systems designed to enhance situational awareness and support operational decision-making. The event also served as an avenue to showcased the company’s weapons portfolio, which include the Q1 Corner rifle and the recently launched BIG556 rifles in 4.5-inch and 7-inch configurations, designed and manufactured in Qatar. Speaking during the exhibition, the Regional General Manager for Africa at Barzan Holdings and Managing Director of DICON-SUR, Engineer Thamer Al Emadi, said the event provided an important platform to engage with key defence stakeholders, demonstrate the company’s technological capabilities and identify areas of collaboration aligned with Nigeria’s defence priorities. He stated: “We are here at AFRIDEX to discuss Nigeria’s defence needs and explore how Barzan Holdings can support them through the supply of modern defence products and services, as well as potential industrial and technology partnerships. ‘‘We are open to developing solutions that address the specific requirements of the Nigerian Defence Forces and contribute to strengthening the country’s sovereign security.” The post FDI: Qatar’s Barzan Holdings seeks to deepen defense partnerships with Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Hôtellerie de luxe : Falibra Group décroche un partenariat avec Hilton pour la construction d’un hôtel DoubleTree de 196 chambres à Conakry
items.description: La société guinéenne de Bâtiment et Travaux publics (BTP) Falibra Group franchit une nouvelle étape dans son développement avec un projet hôtelier d’envergure à Kaloum. En partenariat avec SCF, l’entreprise a signé, le vendredi 30 octobre 2026, un contrat avec le groupe hôtelier international Hilton pour la réalisation du DoubleTree by Hilton à Conakry. Porté par son PDG, Falilou Diallo, ce projet s’inscrit dans la dynamique de développement des infrastructures hôtelières et d’accueil en Guinée. Il marque également une nouvelle perspective de collaboration entre les entreprises locales et les grandes enseignes internationales. Selon les informations communiquées par les promoteurs, le futur établissement comprendra 196 chambres et suites. Il disposera notamment de plusieurs espaces de restauration, d’une piscine extérieure, d’un bassin pour enfants, d’une salle de sport, d’un espace spa et bien-être ainsi que d’un terrain de tennis. L’hôtel prévoit également des infrastructures destinées aux activités professionnelles et événementielles : salles de réunion, espace polyvalent, pelouse extérieure pour les réceptions et centre d’affaires. Autant d’équipements destinés à accueillir une clientèle d’affaires, des touristes et des organisateurs d’événements. À travers cette réalisation annoncée, Falibra Group entend consolider sa présence dans le secteur guinéen du BTP et renforcer son positionnement dans la construction d’infrastructures de standing. Pour la Guinée, l’arrivée annoncée de l’enseigne DoubleTree by Hilton représente une perspective supplémentaire de développement de l’offre hôtelière, avec des retombées attendues sur l’attractivité économique et le tourisme d’affaires. Ce partenariat constitue ainsi une nouvelle étape pour Falibra Group dans son ambition de participer à la réalisation de projets d’infrastructures de grande envergure en Guinée. items.title: ‘Peter Obi can’t do this alone, put in your widow’s mite’ — Yesufu urges Nigerians to fund campaign
items.description: By Nwafor Sunday Activist and ally of Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Aisha Yesufu, has appealed to Nigerians to contribute financially towards funding his 2027 presidential campaign. Yesufu, in a video posted on X on Wednesday, said the former Anambra State governor could not shoulder the financial burden of the campaign alone, urging supporters to embrace citizen-funded politics. “My fellow citizens, Peter Obi cannot do this alone. There is no way we can say that we want to rescue a nation, we want to get back our nation, we want the people to own this nation, and then we say that we are going to leave everything to Mr Peter Obi to fund,” she said. “So please, every one of us, we need you to put in something. Let the citizens fund this election. “Let us be the ones that say our one naira; we go here, and it will be used for this or that.” Recalling the 2023 presidential election, Yesufu said Obi had initially been reluctant to embark on public fundraising but was eventually persuaded that financial contributions would deepen citizens’ involvement in the campaign. “Mr Peter Obi never wanted us to use public fundraising. But I remember saying to him, people need to be involved. And when people give, they are emotionally invested,” she said. She said the fundraising exercise generated contributions from supporters, adding that the accounts were made public and the funds properly accounted for despite criticisms. Yesufu argued that the previous arrangement, under which Obi largely funded campaign activities, was no longer sustainable, insisting that supporters must share the financial responsibility. “It can no longer work. Every one of us has to put in our own widow’s mite,” she said. She, however, clarified that the fundraising initiative was separate from that of the NDC, explaining that the party would announce its own account details for members and supporters willing to contribute directly to its activities. “This is what we, as citizens, are going to use to fund the things that we can do for Mr Peter Obi. The party are going to put out their own accounts,” she said. “Those who want to donate to the party, please wait for their account. This particular account that is here is for Peter Obi’s campaign donated by citizens.” The activist pledged transparency in the management of the contributions, assuring donors that every amount received would be accounted for. “In 2023, I was accountable, and I accounted for every dime. And in 2027, by the grace of God, I will also be accountable. And I will account for every dime,” she said. items.title: Nigeria’s economy sustains growth as PMI rises to 53.2 points
items.description: •Industry, agriculture strengthen expansion; services growth slows By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief Nigeria’s economy sustained its growth momentum in October 2026, with the Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rising to 53.2 points from 53.0 points in September, indicating a fifth consecutive month of expansion in economic activities. The latest PMI report released by the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, yesterday, showed that growth was recorded across the three major sectors of the economy — Industry, Services and Agriculture — although the pace of expansion varied, with Agriculture maintaining its position as the best-performing sector. The report indicated that 24 of the 32 subsectors surveyed expanded during the review month, while eight contracted, pointing to a broad-based improvement in business activities. A breakdown of the sectoral performance showed that the Industry PMI rose to 52.6 points in October from 52.0 points in September, representing a third consecutive month of expansion in industrial activities. Of the 16 industrial subsectors surveyed, 12 recorded expansion, while four contracted. Similarly, the Agriculture PMI increased significantly to 54.7 points from 53.1 points in September, extending the sector’s uninterrupted expansion streak to 27 months. All five agricultural subsectors surveyed recorded growth during the period, making agriculture the strongest-performing sector in the economy. Livestock recorded the highest PMI at 56.4 points, while Agricultural Support Services recorded the lowest at 52.0 points. General Farming Activities, New Orders, Employment and Inventories remained in expansion, at 56.8, 55.6, 52.9 and 53.6 points, respectively However, the Services sector recorded a marginal moderation in growth, as its PMI declined to 52.7 points in October from 53.2 points in September. Despite the decline, the sector sustained its expansion for the fourth consecutive month, with seven of the 11 subsectors surveyed recording growth, while four contracted. Further analysis of the report showed improvements in key indicators of economic activity, including output, new orders, employment and raw materials inventory. The Output Index rose to 53.5 points in October, while the New Orders and Employment indices increased to 52.1 points and 52.7 points, respectively. The Raw Materials Inventory Index also improved to 51.8 points from 51.1 points in September, remaining above the 50-point threshold that separates expansion from contraction. The improvement in new orders and employment suggests that businesses experienced increased demand and continued to expand their workforce during the review period. However, businesses continued to contend with rising costs, as the Composite Input Price Index increased by 0.7 points, while the Output Price Index rose by 0.5 points. A sectoral breakdown showed that input price indices increased in Services and Agriculture but declined in Industry. On the output price front, the indices increased in Industry and Agriculture but declined in Services. The October PMI performance therefore points to a sustained improvement in economic activities, with stronger growth in Industry and Agriculture compensating for the slight moderation in Services. The continued expansion in output, new orders, employment and inventories also indicates improving business conditions, although rising input and output prices remain areas of concern for businesses and policymakers. items.title: North Korea says it tested air-defence missile, staged cruise missile drill
items.description: North Korea test-fired a newly designed air-defence missile system and staged a cruise missile strike drill on Wednesday, state media KCNA reported on Thursday. KCNA said the air-defence test confirmed the technical specifications and reliability of the missile’s new materials and multiple guidance modes. It also confirmed the system’s ability to identify and track targets, KCNA said. A sub-unit of North Korea’s long-range strategic cruise missile unit in the east also struck a virtual airport target in a drill on Wednesday, KCNA said. The KCNA report confirmed a South Korean military statement on Wednesday that Pyongyang fired multiple missiles towards the sea from the Sondok area on the east coast. It was the fourth North Korean weapons launch in a month. A South Korean Defence Ministry official said on Thursday that early detection data suggested the missiles could have been several different types. Images released by Pyongyang appeared to show the cruise missile carrying a cluster warhead, according to Shin Jong-woo, secretary general of the Korea Defense & Security Forum. He said the launch appeared intended to test how effectively the warhead could disperse a payload over a target area. items.title: Interdiction de l’exploitation clandestine de l’or en Guinée : que l’émotion ne prenne pas le dessus sur la raison au Burkina Faso (Par Sayon Mara)
items.description: Depuis l'interdiction de l'exploitation anarchique, sauvage et inadmissible de l'or en Guinée, notamment à Siguiri où les dégâts se font de plus en plus sentir, le gouvernement burkinabé multiplie les communications, donnant l'impression qu'il y a eu expulsion de ses ressortissants en République de Guinée. Or, la réalité est toute autre. Il n'y a eu aucune expulsion, mais plutôt des mesures pour protéger l'environnement et les populations de cette partie de la Guinée. Il faut remettre les choses à leur place, car il n'y a eu ni communiqué ni manifestation des populations guinéennes contre les ressortissants d'un pays étranger en Guinée. Le gouvernement a simplement interdit l'exploitation clandestine de l'or sur ses sols. Quoi de plus normal ! Que l’émotion ne prenne pas le dessus sur la raison au Burkina Faso, car aucune expulsion de Burkinabés n'a eu lieu en Guinée. Le gouvernement guinéen a simplement fermé les sites où cette exploitation sauvage avait lieu. De plus, ce ne sont pas seulement des Burkinabè qui étaient concernés, mais aussi des personnes de plusieurs autres nationalités qui avaient pris goût à l'exploitation clandestine de l'or en Haute-Guinée. Même des Guinéens sont concernés par ces mesures d'interdiction. Les autorités burkinabè ne sauraient admettre ce qui se passe à Siguiri. C'est l'avenir des générations futures qui est menacé. Il est donc tout à fait normal que les autorités guinéennes prennent des mesures face à cette situation inquiétante et révoltante. D'autre part, il serait important que les blogueurs guinéens et burkinabés, en quête de vues, fassent très attention pour éviter toute escalade de violence verbale sur les réseaux sociaux. Depuis toujours, la Guinée entretient de bonnes relations de fraternité avec le Burkina Faso et tous les autres pays africains. Ce n'est pas maintenant que ce climat sera écorché. items.title: FG records N4.69trn fiscal deficit in Q1’26 as revenue falls
items.description: Nigeria’s economy grows 3.89% – Budget Office By Udeme Akpan The Federal Government (FG) recorded an aggregate fiscal deficit of N4.69 trillion in the first quarter of 2026, as revenue generation fell significantly below target, highlighting challenges in financing the 2026 budget. This came as Nigeria’s economy grew by 3.89 per cent in real terms during the quarter, driven by improved performance in the oil and non-oil sectors. Figures from the Budget Office of the Federation (BOF), contained in its 2026 Budget Performance Report, showed that the fiscal deficit was N4.69 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N7.86 trillion for the January–March period, representing N3.18 trillion below projection. The report showed that aggregate Federal Government revenue stood at N5.08 trillion, compared with the quarterly target of N9.22 trillion, resulting in a shortfall of N4.14 trillion. This represented about 55 per cent of projected revenue. Similarly, aggregate government expenditure amounted to N9.76 trillion, against the projected N17.08 trillion, indicating an underperformance of N7.32 trillion, or about 57.2 per cent of the target. On deficit financing, domestic borrowing stood at N3.9 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N4.61 trillion, leaving a shortfall of N704.03 billion. However, foreign borrowing, projected at N2.70 trillion for the quarter, recorded no actual inflow during the period. The Federal Government also realised N287.44 billion from multilateral and bilateral project-tied loans, against the quarterly target of N512.23 billion, while privatisation proceeds stood at N3.32 billion, compared with the projected N47.29 billion. The figures highlight the government’s difficulties in generating sufficient revenue and accessing planned financing sources to support budget implementation. Nigeria’s economy grows 3.89% On economic performance, the Budget Office reported that the oil sector grew by 2.57 per cent year-on-year in real terms during the first quarter, up by 0.70 percentage points from 1.87 per cent recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The non-oil sector expanded by 3.94 per cent, outperforming the oil sector and accounting for a larger share of the economy’s growth. The Budget Office described the performance as “a period of macroeconomic stabilisation accompanied by moderate real-sector expansion.” However, it identified weak, although improving, revenue performance as a major constraint to budget execution, noting that the Federal Government continued to meet its non-discretionary expenditure obligations. It stated: “Improving revenue collections in the subsequent quarters of the year is critical to the successful execution of the 2026 Budget.” The report said the government would intensify efforts to improve economic growth and revenue generation, while controlling recurrent expenditure, particularly personnel costs. On strategies to strengthen the economy, the Budget Office identified oil production recovery, tax-base expansion, improved tax compliance, increased domestic production, agricultural productivity, infrastructure development, private-sector credit and export diversification as key priorities. It stated: “The central policy challenge for the remainder of 2026 is therefore not simply to preserve stability, but to convert stability into higher productive capacity and stronger domestic revenue mobilisation.” The report further explained that consolidating gains in inflation management, exchange-rate stability and the external sector would require creating sufficient room for productive private-sector credit, investment and employment generation. It added that controlling recurrent expenditure, particularly personnel costs, and addressing security challenges remained important to improving fiscal performance. On budget implementation, the Budget Office reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to transparency and accountability, stating that it would ensure “firm adherence to budget implementation guidelines and the governance framework on monitoring of capital budget implementation.” It added that efforts would focus on improving budget execution efficiency and ensuring effective project management in the remaining quarters of 2026. items.title: Le reflux populiste, principale leçon de l’échec des Démocrates américains
items.description: L’échec des Démocrates américains portés par le président populiste Donal Trump démontre que les promesses démagogiques trahies finissent inéluctablement par se payer au prix fort. Que le mécontentement populaire s’exprime par la contestation de rue ou par la souveraineté des urnes, le décalage entre la rhétorique national-populiste et la détérioration concrète des conditions de vie socio-économiques engendre un retour de bâton, comme celui auquel nous assistons aux Etats-Unis. (Photo : La victoire historique d’Abdul Rahmane Mohamed El-Sayed au Sénat dans le Michigan illustre la faillite des méthodes populistes de Donald Trump.) Elyes Kasri * Avec le raz de marée démocrate à la Chambre des Représentants et au Sénat, les élections législatives de mi-mandat de novembre 2026 aux États-Unis transcendent le simple cadre des scrutins intermédiaires pour s’inscrire comme le pivot d’un phénomène mondial de rejet du populisme, caractérisé par l’érosion du pouvoir d’achat, la politique-spectacle et la personnalisation excessive du pouvoir. Face à une gouvernance républicaine jugée coupable de duplicité et d’inféodation aux puissances financières ainsi qu’à des intérêts extérieurs, le corps électoral américain a manifesté une sentence sans équivoque, dont l’amplitude varie à l’échelle internationale selon la résilience et le caractère démocratique des institutions en place. Malgré les critiques récurrentes inhérentes aux structures institutionnelles américaines, le verdict des urnes a produit un véritable tsunami démocrate au Congrès. La reprise conjointe de la Chambre des représentants et du Sénat sonne comme le désaveu cinglant de la politique de Donald Trump. Cette bérézina républicaine s'est concrétisée en dépit des manœuvres désespérées de dernière minute de l’exécutif, notamment l’annonce opportuniste de mettre fin à l’aide militaire américaine à Israël — estimée à 4 milliards de dollars par an — pour capter l’électorat pacifiste. L’homme à abattre pour le lobby pro-israélien américain Symbole ultime de ce basculement de l’opinion publique, la victoire historique d’ Abdul Rahmane Mohamed El-Sayed au Sénat dans le Michigan illustre la faillite des méthodes populistes. Malgré une campagne agressive orchestrée par le sommet de l’État américain et le déversement massif de 437,5 millions de dollars par des PAC républicains et des lobbys pro-israéliens, la résistance démocratique locale a triomphé de la ploutocratie électorale. Cette dynamique démontre que les promesses démagogiques trahies finissent inéluctablement par se payer au prix fort. Que le mécontentement populaire s’exprime par la contestation de rue — comme en France et au sein d’autres nations européennes — ou par la souveraineté des urnes comme aux États-Unis, le décalage entre la rhétorique national-populiste et la détérioration concrète des conditions de vie socio-économiques engendre un retour de bâton électoral. En dernière analyse, cette transition souligne une vérité systémique cruciale : dans les pays aux régimes politiques verrouillés, l’absence de soupapes de sécurité démocratiques et d’alternance institutionnelle ne fait que différer l’inévitable. L’étouffement des contestations légitimes ne peut que radicaliser les crises futures, alourdissant à terme la facture politique et sociale de la gouvernance despotique. * Ancien ambassadeur. L’article Le reflux populiste, principale leçon de l’échec des Démocrates américains est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Ghana, Trinidad and Tobago explore joint mechanism for reparatory justice
items.description: Ghana and Trinidad and Tobago are exploring the establishment of a dedicated mechanism, potentially co-chaired by the African Union (AU) and the Caribbean Community (CARICOM), to advance the reparatory justice agenda and facilitate structured engagement with the United Kingdom (UK). The proposal was discussed at a bilateral meeting between Mr Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Ghana’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, and his Trinidad and Tobago counterpart, Mr Sean S.M. Sobers, on the sidelines of the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda. The discussions focused on strengthening bilateral relations, deepening Africa-Caribbean cooperation and advancing their shared campaign for reparatory justice. The two Ministers observed that existing platforms, including the Commonwealth Foreign Affairs Ministers Meeting, might be too broad to accommodate focused and sustained discussions on reparatory justice. They, therefore, underscored the need for a dedicated platform to provide a more coordinated approach to engagement with the UK and other relevant international partners. They stressed that reparatory justice should extend beyond financial compensation to include acknowledgement of historical injustices, reconciliation, guarantees of non-repetition and efforts towards a fairer international order. The Ministers also highlighted the need to leverage the current UK administration’s reported openness to the issue while safeguarding the fundamental principles of the reparatory justice agenda. The Trinidad and Tobago delegation proposed development-oriented interventions as part of the reparatory process, including expanded scholarship opportunities, support for healthcare infrastructure and hospital development, and improvements in educational facilities. Climate-related cooperation was also identified as a potential area for consideration under the broader framework. The proposed mechanism comes against the backdrop of Ghana’s growing international campaign for reparatory justice, which recorded a significant diplomatic milestone in March 2026 following the adoption of a resolution by the United Nations General Assembly. On March 25, 2026, the UN General Assembly adopted Resolution A/RES/80/250, recognising the trafficking of enslaved Africans and racialised chattel enslavement as the gravest crime against humanity. The resolution, spearheaded by President John Dramani Mahama in his capacity as the AU Champion on Reparations, received 123 votes in favour, three against and 52 abstentions. The adoption marked a significant step in Ghana’s efforts to elevate historical injustices into a global conversation on accountability, healing and reparative action. Subsequently, Ghana hosted a High-Level Consultative Conference on the Next Steps to the UN Resolution in Accra from June 17 to 19, 2026, bringing together international stakeholders to develop a practical roadmap for advancing the reparations agenda. President Mahama also announced the establishment of three international panels: the Global Advisory Panel on Reparatory Justice, the Expert Panel on the Restitution of Cultural Artefacts and the Global Legal Panel on Reparatory Justice, to provide strategic, technical and legal support for the process. Ghana has also developed a draft five-year action plan focusing on diplomatic engagement, reparative financing and reforms to the global financial architecture to move the campaign from advocacy to implementation. The latest discussions with Trinidad and Tobago follow renewed diplomatic engagement with the UK. On November 3, 2026, Mr Ablakwa commended the UK for its reported willingness to consider a formal apology and structured dialogue on reparatory justice. He described the development as an important step towards healing, reconciliation and addressing the enduring consequences of the transatlantic slave trade. He said Ghana, together with its partners in the AU, CARICOM and the wider international community, was prepared to work with the UK towards genuine reconciliation, restitution and reparations. On bilateral and multilateral cooperation, the Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to sustaining the longstanding bonds of solidarity between the two countries. They identified Ghana’s anticipated leadership role within the AU in 2027 and Trinidad and Tobago’s forthcoming chairmanship of CARICOM in January 2028 as strategic opportunities to strengthen Africa-Caribbean relations and advance the reparatory justice agenda. The meeting also discussed prospective high-level exchanges, including an invitation to Mr Ablakwa to visit Trinidad and Tobago in 2027 to formally commission the relevant diplomatic mission. The proposed visit would also provide an opportunity to commemorate the 60th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries. The Ministers expressed satisfaction with the discussions and reaffirmed their commitment to deepening bilateral relations, strengthening Africa-Caribbean cooperation and pursuing shared interests through multilateral engagements, particularly on reparatory justice.

items.title: Council of State requires a revamp – Avoka
items.description: Cletus Avoka, a former Majority Leader of Parliament, has called for an independent and adequately resourced Council of State, arguing that its current structure constrains its effectiveness. He said separating the Council from the machinery of government was essential to strengthening its role in Ghana’s democratic governance framework. Speaking at a roundtable organised by the Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA) on constitutional reforms, Mr Avoka, who is also a Member of the Council of State, said the institution required greater autonomy and dedicated funding. “The Council of State needs revamping and its own financial arrangements, so that it will have the power to operate on its own,” he said. Mr Avoka said the Council had remained largely stagnant despite developments in other state institutions, including Parliament. “While Parliament is developing and progressing, the Council is virtually stagnant in the sense that there are no offices for members. Only the Chairman has an office. “The others, they are behaving like the 1993 Parliament – you carry your office in your car boots,” he said. Former Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo emphasised the need to advance the constitutional review process to improve governance outcomes. “Democracy is not just an engine itself, but it leads to development, sustainable, effective and desirable development. “How are we going to do that under this present constitution? I think it has proven rather difficult,” she said. Mr Sam Okudzeto, an eminent legal practitioner who chaired the roundtable, commended the IEA for facilitating the discussion and urged continued national dialogue on constitutional reforms. The programme was held on the theme: “Views and Reflections: The Prempeh Committee’s Report and Government’s Position on Constitutional Review.” The Constitution Review Committee, chaired by Professor Henry Prempeh, was established in January 2025 to undertake a comprehensive review of the 1992 Constitution. Its mandate includes identifying constitutional gaps, implementation challenges and governance constraints, and proposing reforms to strengthen accountability, inclusion, democratic governance and national development. The Committee’s recommendations cover nine thematic areas, including a more accountable presidency, people-centred democracy, public sector reforms, decentralisation, social justice, constitutional adaptability, national security, and strengthened accountability and justice institutions.

items.title: Ghana to establish 21,000-tonne grain storage facility in Upper West
items.description: The Ministry of Food and Agriculture has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with DMT Collateral Management to establish a 21,000-metric-tonne grain storage facility in the Upper West Region. The project, expected to be completed by August 2027, will involve the construction of silos in Wa to reduce post-harvest losses, improve food storage capacity and strengthen national food security. The facility is also expected to support the Government’s Feed Ghana Programme by providing storage infrastructure for increased production of rice and maize, while maintaining emergency grain reserves. Mr Paul Minlah, Managing Director of DMT Collateral Management, said the project would include a designated food security hub and an emergency reserve facility, which he described as a “hospital bin” to provide food supplies during emergencies. He said the company would lead the technical and commercial development of the project, mobilise financing and work with a joint project implementation committee to ensure its successful delivery. Mr Minlah said the equipment and construction component of the project was backed by an export credit facility of approximately €4.8 million, with an additional investment of about US$5 million. He noted that the project would also build local capacity through the training of National Service personnel, Feed Ghana Brigadiers and Ghanaian technicians in silo operations, grain drying, quality management and maintenance. Mr Eric Opoku, Minister of Food and Agriculture, said the facility would help address the country’s inadequate storage infrastructure, which remained a challenge despite increased production of rice and maize. He explained that although the National Food Buffer Stock Company had resources to procure food from farmers, it lacked sufficient warehouse and storage capacity to accommodate the produce. Mr Opoku said the Ministry would support the implementation of the project and ensure that technical personnel, National Service personnel and Feed Ghana Brigadiers participated in the training programmes. He described the Wa facility as the first phase of a broader national storage infrastructure expansion programme, indicating that the Government was considering the establishment of between 15 and 20 similar facilities across the country. The Minister urged DMT Collateral Management to commence implementation promptly to enable the Ministry to align its activities with the project’s timelines. In a related development, Omanbapa AgriTech Limited presented publicity materials, including banners, branded souvenirs and flyers, to support the 42nd National Farmers’ Day celebration scheduled for December 4, 2026, in Sunyani, the Bono Regional capital. Mr Opoku commended the company for fulfilling its commitment and appealed to other institutions and corporate organisations to support the celebration to ensure its success.

items.title: Trump says Hegseth doing 'a very good job' as questions swirl about defence secretary's future
items.description: US President Donald Trump backed Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth a day after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in midterm elections that reflected voter anger over the war on Iran. Asked whether he was considering replacing Hegseth, whom he has described as a champion of the war, Trump told reporters: “No, I think he’s doing a very good job.” The response contrasted with then-president George Bush, who fired Defence Secretary Donald Rumsfeld the morning after the 2006 midterm elections, when voter discontent over the Iraq war helped Democrats win control of Congress. But sources said Trump could still replace Hegseth as Republicans assess their losses. One Trump adviser said Hegseth “could be on the chopping block” because of the war. “Someone is going to get blamed for this and you know it’s not going to be him (Trump),” the adviser said. Trump has described Hegseth as a key proponent of the unpopular conflict, saying on March 23: “Pete, I think you were the first one to speak up, and you said, ‘Let’s do it, because you can’t let them have a nuclear weapon.’” On Wednesday, Vice President JD Vance publicly questioned whether the Iran war was worth it and said it cost Republicans control of Congress. Asked for comment, the White House referred Reuters to Trump’s public remarks on Hegseth. The Defence Department said Hegseth was “100 percent committed” to leading the Pentagon until the end of Trump’s term, which ends on Jan. 20, 2029. Impeachment threat Hegseth has been a polarising figure in American politics and has made adversaries even with his own Republican Party. One Republican lawmaker, US Representative Thomas Massie, even filed articles of impeachment against him earlier this year, accusing him of abusing his office by launching hostilities against Iran without approval by Congress. Republican US Senator Thom Tillis told CBS News on Tuesday night that Hegseth has “a reckoning” coming and his strained relationship with lawmakers was undermining the Trump administration’s push for a $1.5 trillion defence spending package in Congress. “I think after the election, we need to determine whether or not he’s the best person to bring those needs to Congress if he wants something done before the end of this Congress, which is only 60 days away,” Tillis said as the midterm results came in. Democrats have promised to investigate Hegseth and his handling of the Pentagon, and aides say that could include everything from his handling of the Iran war to his purges of top military officers including the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. He could also face scrutiny over his Ukraine policy and US military strikes on suspected drug trafficking boats in Latin American waters, which some Democrats say could amount to war crimes. At times, the conflict between Hegseth and members of Congress has become personal. Last year, Hegseth sought to prosecute Democratic US Senator Mark Kelly after he and five other Democrats in Congress with backgrounds in the military and intelligence urged US troops to refuse illegal orders. Hegseth accused them of sedition. Representative Adam Smith, the Democrat who is expected to lead the House Armed Services Committee next year, promised vigorous oversight on everything from the Iran war to what he called the erosion of the “apolitical foundation of the armed forces”. A source familiar with the matter said rancour on Capitol Hill over Hegseth has featured in White House discussions about potential replacements for him, saying there would be a need to have someone in the job who could distance themselves from events under Democratic scrutiny. Chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said Hegseth would continue to drive Trump’s agenda and that the Pentagon “has followed the law”. “Secretary Hegseth will not back down or be deterred by politicians seeking to score partisan points or launch phony investigations where no wrongdoing exists,” Parnell said. Tennessee Senate seat? One long-rumoured possibility for Hegseth would be filling the Senate seat that will be vacated by Senator Marsha Blackburn, who was elected on Tuesday to become Tennessee’s next governor starting in January. She has four years left in her term, and Hegseth, a Tennessee resident who voted there on Tuesday, could be appointed to the position, without having to run for election. Asked whether he wanted Hegseth to fill Blackburn’s seat, Trump said: “Well, I think, I think he’s doing a very good job, and I actually think he’d be very popular if he did that.” “But I haven’t heard that at all,” Trump told reporters. Trump has regularly praised Hegseth publicly, and has given the former Army National Guard soldier significant leeway as he sought to reshape the Pentagon. But last month Trump publicly split with Hegseth by pulling the plug on his plans to livestream the Army’s firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan.

items.description: Le Président de l’Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP), Ousmane Bougouma, a visité les stands des régions, le village de l’Alliance des Etats du Sahel (AES) ainsi que le village artisanal, le mercredi 4 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Le Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO) continue de mettre en lumière la créativité et le savoir-faire des artisans africains. A cet effet, le Président de l’Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP), Ousmane Bougouma, s’est rendu sur le site du salon pour découvrir les différentes réalisations expo-sées, notamment dans les stands des régions, le village de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel (AES) et le village artisanal. Une visite qui, selon lui, vise à encourager les artisans africains en général et ceux du Burkina Faso en parti-culier. A l’issue de sa tournée, il s’est dit impressionné par la qualité des œuvres découvertes qui témoignent du génie créateur des artisans locaux, de leur savoir-faire et de leur ingéniosité. Le président de l’ALP a rappelé que le thème de cette 18e édition, revêt une importance particulière dans le contexte actuel de recherche de la souveraineté économique. « Et cette souveraineté économique ne peut se faire qu’à travers une industrialisation qui a besoin d’organisation des différents secteurs d’acti-vité », a-t-il précisé. Par ailleurs, l’Assemblée législative du Peuple entend apporter sa contribution à la valorisation du secteur à travers deux catégories de prix spéciaux. Le premier, dénommé prix Thomas-Sankara de la créativité, d’un montant global de 3 millions de francs CFA, vise à magnifier l’ingéniosité et l’innovation des artisans. « Et rappeler aussi que le capitaine Thomas Sankara a porté le flambeau des artisans et nous devons travailler à ce que ce flambeau-là ne s’éteigne jamais », a-t-il évoqué. Le second prix, de 3 millions 250 000 francs CFA appelé prix des régions, concerne les 17 stands régionaux visités par la délégation. « Il s’agit surtout d’encourager la créativité de nos artisans dans les différentes régions. Donc, nous sommes venus non seulement saluer le travail de nos artisans mais rappeler que l’artisanat participe à notre souveraineté économique », a-t-il expliqué. Ousmane Bougouma a, au terme de sa visite souhaité une bonne édition aux participants et invité la population à effectuer le déplacement au SIAO. Il l’a notamment exhortée à découvrir les œuvres exposées et à pri-vilégier la consommation des produits locaux. Une démarche qui, selon lui, permettra aux artisans de contribuer davantage à l’économie nationale. Wendyam Pascaline KALMOGO

items.title: Race for 2028 heats up after US midterms firestorm
items.description: President Donald Trump’s stunning midterms defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election — the race to replace him in the White House in 2028. The crushing defeat for the Republicans is particularly stinging for Vice President JD Vance, who had been the frontrunner but now risks being seen as tied to his lame-duck boss. But the midterms are a potential launchpad for rising Democratic stars like Georgia senator Jon Ossoff, whose youthful vibe has already drawn comparisons to former president Barack Obama. Republicans in turmoil The MAGA coalition that shot Trump to power in 2016 and 2024 effectively collapsed in Tuesday’s midterms, leaving any presumptive Republican heir with a mountain to climb. Long seen as the odds-on favorite for the Republican nomination in 2028, Vance is the most obvious victim after hitching his wagon to Trump throughout the midterms campaigns with rallies in swing states. The ambitious 42-year-old quickly tried to distance himself from the electoral disaster, blaming it on Trump’s unpopular war on Iran in a long thesis posted on X on Wednesday. But voters are likely to reject his attempts to disown Trump. It’s a familiar problem for US vice presidents. Former Democratic candidate and vice president Kamala Harris suffered from a similar problem in 2024 when she said that “there’s not a thing that comes to mind” when asked how she’d differentiate herself from Joe Biden. “The bad news for Vance is that sitting vice presidents seldom win the presidency,” James Lindsay of the Council for Foreign Relations, said. Trump’s Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s name has also been bandied about. Rubio, 55, has kept a far lower profile during the midterms but any top official in Trump’s administration will struggle to wash their hands of the Iran war. The Republicans’ midterm disaster could, however, be a boost for other possible candidates. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, 48, who ran against Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024, has suddenly become very vocal. He described the Democratic sweep as “the political equivalent of a meteor strike” — and pointed out that it was only in his own state that Republicans held them off. Texas Senator Ted Cruz, 55, has also left the door open, having run against Trump in 2016 — although his chances may have been harmed by the Democrats’ stunning senate and governor wins in the midterms in his state. Democrats on a high The Democratic field is crowded but the midterms have given some likely candidates a boost. Ossoff’s reelection as Georgia Senator has fueled speculation about a 2028 run by a telegenic politician who has already gained attention for mocking Trump’s relationship with a young staffer. The 39-year-old has said that he has “zero interest in running for president” but his swiftly-declared win in Georgia — and his victory speech — have bolstered his status in the party. Before the midterms Kamala Harris, 62, had been the favorite for the nomination, but there are many in the party who would prefer to have someone without a losing track record. Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, 53, who was interviewed by Harris to be her running mate in 2024, had a good night on Tuesday as he stormed back to reelection in the key battleground state. Outgoing California Governor Gavin Newsom, 59, is another big name who has repeatedly taken on Trump. He predicted in an interview with AFP in September Trump’s presidency “as we know it would be over after the midterms. But Newsom, like Harris, may be seen as more of an old guard figure in a party that is looking to its rising stars. A prominent but potentially divisive choice would be left-wing New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who said in September that she was weighing a run, musing about whether a Latina could win in a country that rejected female nominees in 2016 and 2024. Other possible contenders include former Chicago mayor Rahm Emmanuel, JB Pritzker, the billionaire Illinois governor who set out a lengthy national agenda after winning a third term on Tuesday, Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear, and Arizona senator and former astronaut Mark Kelly.

items.title: CHOGM 2026: Prioritise human rights over political convenience — Onoh tells Bianca
items.description: By Emma Nnadozie Denge (Dr) Josef Onoh, former Southeast spokesman to President Bola Tinubu, has congratulated the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, on her appointment as Vice-Chair of the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group (CMAG). Onoh, who is also Chairman of the Forum of Former Members of the Enugu State House of Assembly, urged his elder sister to use her new position to promote democratic governance, institutional accountability and human rights across Africa. The appointment was confirmed at the 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM 2026) in Antigua and Barbuda. In a statement issued from Oman, Onoh described the appointment as a recognition of Odumegwu-Ojukwu’s diplomatic experience, intellect and commitment to justice, equity and the rule of law. He said the appointment was a source of pride to their family and a recognition of her years of service to Nigeria. “This prestigious elevation on the global stage is a well-deserved recognition of your years of dedicated service to our nation,” Onoh said. He added that her new responsibility within the 56-member Commonwealth presented an opportunity to advance accountable and democratic leadership. Recognising the demands of the office, Onoh urged the minister to remain committed to principled diplomacy, particularly at a time when Africa faces critical governance and human rights challenges. He also appealed to her to uphold the values of integrity, courage and truth, which he said were part of the legacy of their late parents. Onoh cautioned against sacrificing those values for short-term political interests, stressing that public office should be guided by humanity and service. “Let your tenure be defined by the rare virtues of humility, deep empathy, and a steadfast dedication to humanity,” he said. “Politics and political offices are fleeting, but the impact we make on human lives and the integrity with which we serve endure forever. Always place the well-being of humanity far above the allure of political office.” He expressed confidence in her ability to discharge the new responsibility, while praying for wisdom, strength and divine protection as she assumes the assignment. Onoh said he hoped her leadership would bring further honour to their family, Nigeria and the African continent. items.title: Retrait des permis de conduire : une quarantaine de dossiers examinée
items.description: La Direction générale des transports terrestres et maritimes (DGTTM) a tenu la troisième session foraine de la Commission technique spéciale de retrait du permis de conduire (CTSRPC), le lundi 26 octobre 2026, à la gare routière de Boromo. L’ouverture de la session de 48h a été présidée par le haut-commissaire de la province, Martin Bado, représentant le gouverneur de la région de Bankui. Après les gares routières de Tampouy à Ouagadougou et de Pouytenga dans la province du Kouritenga, l’honneur a échu à la gare routière de Boromo, important pôle de transport et de mobilité dans la province des Balé, région de Bankui, d’accueillir, du 26 au 27 octobre 2026, la 3e session foraine de la Commission technique spéciale de retrait du permis de conduire (CTSRPC). L’activité a été placée sous la présidence du gouverneur de la région, représenté par le haut-commissaire de la province des Balé, Martin Bado. Elle a réuni une diversité d’acteurs dont des conducteurs mis en cause, les différentes composantes d’acteurs du domaine de la mobilité, des procureurs de tribunaux de grande instance, la gendarmerie et la police nationale et des experts de la sécurité routière. L’objectif de la session a été de faciliter le renforcement de la sécurité routière par le rapprochement de la CTSRPC des usagers et des acteurs provinciaux et régionaux à travers l’examen des dossiers à elle soumis et la conduite d’actions de sensibilisation sur les risques d’accidents de la circulation. En effet, elle s’est penchée, au cours des 48h, sur une quarantaine de dossiers liés à des accidents de circulation dont 28 ont concerné les régions de Bankui et du Sourou. Le directeur régional chargé des transports, Souleymane Zongo, a relevé que les dossiers soumis à la commission sont des procès-verbaux de tribunaux impliquant des chauffeurs auteurs d’accidents « graves ». Les experts auront la charge d’analyser ces dossiers en examen afin de proposer des avis. Donner de la visibilité à la commission Le directeur de la circulation routière et de la normalisation à la Direction générale des transports terrestres et maritimes (DGTTM), Baowendmanegré Zoungrana, représentant le directeur général, a soutenu que la CTSRPC a en charge d’examiner des dossiers et des procès-verbaux d’accidents, de donner des orientations et de formuler des recommandations. Il a précisé qu’il peut arriver que la commission propose la suspension du permis de conduire, son retrait ou sa restitution ou encore un recyclage du mis en cause. A l’en croire, le choix de Boromo s’explique par sa position stratégique de ville traversée par la RN 1et le constat d’événements malheureux liés à l’insécurité routière dans la zone. Face à cela, la DGTTM a opté d’approcher la population de cette localité afin de la sensibiliser pour une conduite responsable et plus sûre sur les routes, a expliqué celui qui a affirmé que la session ne vise pas seulement la répression. Le représentant du syndicat des transporteurs routiers, Issouf Soma, et l’un des chauffeurs mis en cause, Ismaël Yamponi, apprécient positivement l’organisation de cette session qui contribue au recadrage et à la maîtrise des règles et du Code de la route. Le président de la délégation spéciale de Boromo, Isaï Wenonga Bamogo, a indiqué que l’organisation de la présente session crée une proximité entre les institutions et les populations et favorise des échanges avec les acteurs locaux du transport routier. Il a déclaré que la sécurité routière concerne tout le monde. Elle exige alors de la vigilance, du respect des règles et de la responsabilité partagée. Présidant l’ouverture de cette 3e session, le représentant du gouverneur, Martin Bado, a rappelé les statistiques du ministère de la Sécurité qui font état de 15 853 accidents de circulation, dont 12 858 blessés, et 910 décès enregistrés au Burkina Faso entre le 1er janvier et le 30 septembre 2026. Pour inverser la tendance, le gouvernement a multiplié les actions en faveur de la sécurité routière, dont le renforcement du cadre réglementaire de la CTSRPC. « La mise en place et l’opérationnalisation de cette commission visent à instaurer la discipline sur nos routes et à responsabiliser les conduc-teurs », a déclaré le haut-commissaire des Balé. Il a conclu que la tenue de cette session foraine se propose de rendre visible la CTSRPC qui, malgré son rôle stratégique, reste peu connue du grand public. Yacouba BELEM

items.title: Kasseh Market sweepers begin strike over three months’ unpaid salaries
items.description: About 27 sweepers at the Kasseh Market in the Ada East District of the Greater Accra Region have embarked on an indefinite strike over three months of unpaid salaries. The workers began the industrial action on Monday, November 2, 2026, demanding payment of their outstanding salaries before returning to work. Some of the workers, who spoke to the Ghana News Agency (GNA) on condition of anonymity for fear of victimisation, said delays in the payment of their salaries had become a recurring problem, with some payments remaining outstanding for extended periods. They said they worked for about two years under the previous administration without receiving their salaries. According to them, during the 2024 election campaign, some National Democratic Congress (NDC) leaders promised to increase their monthly remuneration from GH¢250 to GH¢700, a commitment they said motivated them to continue working diligently. They, however, alleged that after the new administration assumed office, they worked for another 10 months without payment. They said when they approached the authorities over the outstanding salaries, they were informed that there was no formal agreement with them to warrant payment for the period. The workers said the assembly’s leadership subsequently invited them to a meeting and asked them to resume work, during which their monthly remuneration was increased from GH¢250 to GH¢350. They, however, said they had not received their salaries for the past three months and had not received any formal communication explaining the delay, prompting their decision to suspend work. “We do not want another issue with our payment because most of us are ageing and still have children and families to cater for. If you cannot pay us the GH¢700 promised, at least pay us the GH¢350 for the work we do,” one of the workers said. They stated that they had endured prolonged unfair treatment and were determined not to continue working without receiving their due remuneration. Some of the workers also expressed concern about alleged intimidation whenever they spoke to the media about their working conditions. “Anytime we speak with the media, they start calling and threatening us. Occasionally, they accuse us of aligning with the opposition to disgrace them,” another worker alleged. Meanwhile, a visit by the GNA to the market on Wednesday revealed heaps of refuse accumulating following the Tuesday market activities, including used plastic bags, leftover food, plastic waste and other discarded materials. The situation had left parts of the market littered and unpleasant, raising concerns about sanitation and the potential health implications for traders, shoppers and other users of the facility. Mr Kenneth Kabu Kofi Kanor, District Chief Executive (DCE) for Ada East, declined to comment when contacted by the GNA on the matter.

items.title: Peter Obi’s Bayelsa visit triggers political realignment as Ijaw leaders demand devt, unity
items.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The political landscape of Bayelsa State is undergoing a seismic shift following last week’s visit of Mr. Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC’s presidential candidate, to the heart of the Ijaw Nation. This development, stakeholders said, has introduced a new dimension into the evolving political configuration of the state and the wider Niger Delta ahead of the 2027 general elections. Read Also: * Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar * LP chieftain Arabambi sues CCB over Obi’s asset declaration * Gunmen attack ADC guber candidate’s convoy in Sokoto, candidate escapes Obi’s visit, which coincided with the homecoming of Senator Henry Seriake Dickson as National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, featured the commissioning of the NDC state secretariat in Yenagoa, high-level political engagements with stakeholders, and a spectacular traditional Ijaw war canoe and boat regatta at Toru-Orua in Sagbama Local Government Area. Political analysts and Ijaw leaders who spoke to our correspondent described the developments as more than ceremonial, saying they signal the beginning of fresh political alignments and realignments that could reshape the state’s political architecture. Delivering a penetrating analysis, Professor Benjamin Okaba, a university don and immediate past President of the Ijaw National Congress, INC, said Obi’s visit “has introduced another significant dimension into the evolving political configuration of Bayelsa State and, by extension, the Ijaw Nation.” Okaba, who recalled his 2024 Bayelsa State Annual Thanksgiving remarks on political alignment and realignment, emphasized that while political affiliations may change, “our identity, history and collective aspirations as an Ijaw people must remain constant.” He said Senator Dickson’s emergence as NDC National Leader “introduces a new dimension into Bayelsa politics,” noting that his experience as a former governor and serving senator gives the party an important political foothold. However, he cautioned that “the success of any political platform must depend on its policies, credibility and commitment to the people’s welfare, not merely political structures or personalities.” Cultural Renaissance, Political Symbolism The traditional boat regatta at Toru-Orua, according to Okaba, underscored the importance of Ijaw cultural identity in political engagement. But he stressed that “celebrating our culture must go beyond ceremonial participation. Political leaders must demonstrate sustained commitment to the welfare, security and development of our riverine communities.” On Obi’s comments regarding federal attention to Bayelsa, Okaba said they “raise important questions about the marginalisation of oil-producing communities. Our people deserve environmental restoration, improved infrastructure, quality education, healthcare and equitable benefits from the resources extracted from their ancestral territories.” The former INC president also highlighted the proposal for a Bayelsa seaport, particularly the long-standing Agge aspiration, insisting it “deserves serious consideration.” He added: “Beyond crude oil, the Ijaw Nation must explore its maritime, agricultural, fisheries and tourism potentials to create employment and stimulate sustainable economic development.” On security, Okaba called for an integrated strategy to tackle kidnapping, piracy and other criminal activities, noting that “effective policing must be complemented by infrastructure, education, youth empowerment and employment opportunities. Sustainable security cannot be separated from sustainable development.” In what appears to be a major policy intervention, Okaba advocated an Ijaw Development Compact involving political parties, elected representatives, traditional institutions, the INC, civil society organisations, professional groups and youth organisations. “The purpose should be to identify and articulate common developmental priorities for the Ijaw Nation and establish measurable commitments against which political parties and elected representatives can be assessed,” he said, adding that such a compact should address environmental restoration, infrastructure, education, healthcare, economic diversification, youth development, resource control, security and political representation. “It should not be another ceremonial document. It should provide a practical framework for engagement, advocacy, monitoring and accountability.” In a direct message to the NDC and the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, Okaba advised both parties to “move beyond partisan antagonism and make the development of Bayelsa State and the wider Ijaw territory the central focus of their political engagements.” He listed critical areas both parties must address: environmental justice and ecological restoration; infrastructure and connectivity; education and healthcare; youth empowerment and employment; economic diversification; resource control and fiscal federalism; security and social stability; and political inclusion and representation. “The political contest should not be about who organises the largest rally, commands the biggest political following, displays the most billboards or attracts the greatest number of traditional boats during a regatta. It should be about who has the most credible ideas for transforming the lives of our people,” he declared. Looking ahead to 2027, Okaba urged Ijaw politicians to appreciate the enormous responsibility that comes with political leadership. “The NDC has an opportunity to demonstrate that it can provide a credible alternative to existing political arrangements. The APC has an opportunity to demonstrate that its access to federal power can translate into meaningful development for Bayelsa and the Niger Delta. Other political parties equally have a responsibility to present credible alternatives and contribute constructively to the political process. “However, none of these political opportunities should be pursued at the expense of the unity and collective aspirations of the Ijaw Nation. We must not allow the 2027 elections to become another occasion for deepening historical divisions, encouraging political hostility or weakening our collective bargaining power.” He added: “The Ijaw Nation needs political leaders who understand that their political fortunes are temporary, but the future of our people is enduring.” Obi’s Visit: A Strategic Masterstroke – Clarkson Also speaking, Amaebi Clarkson, a lawyer and former National Spokesman of the Movement for the Survival of the Ijaw Ethnic Nationality in the Niger Delta, MOSIEND, described Obi’s visit as “very remarkable and strategic, particularly the colourful display of omu aru, the traditional Ijaw war canoe mounted by Ijaw warriors.” “It is a rare gesture accorded to a non-Ijaw. Bayelsa State, being the epicentre of the Ijaw Nation, has a wide influence in the Niger Delta, and Obi’s perceived endorsement in the heart of Ijaw will carry a significant impact in the South-South,” Clarkson said. He noted that beyond the fanfare, the visit “shows Obi’s energetic persona as someone ready to dare the challenges confronting the country. Luckily, the leader of his party, Senator Seriake Dickson, is a man of strong character who is capable of leading the charge in the campaigns. “But above all, Obi’s visit galvanized the massive Igbo presence in Yenagoa, and he is likely to harvest a substantial number of their votes.” The Bigger Picture As the political tempo gathers pace, the message from Bayelsa is unmistakable: the Ijaw Nation is demanding a new kind of politics, one that transcends partisan boundaries and places development, unity and collective destiny at its core. Whether the NDC, APC and other parties will heed this call remains to be seen. But one thing is clear, the forthcoming elections will not just be about who occupies the Creek Haven in Yenagoa. It will be about who can best articulate and deliver on the aspirations of a people long denied the full benefits of their God-given resources. items.description: The naira is trading at different rates against the US dollar across Nigeria’s official and parallel foreign exchange markets on Thursday, November 5, 2026. In the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the dollar is valued at approximately ₦1,347.30, based on the latest reported official rate. At the parallel market, Bureau De Change (BDC) operators are buying the dollar at approximately ₦1,380 and selling at ₦1,390. The figures indicate that Nigerians buying dollars through the parallel market are paying more than those accessing foreign exchange through the official window. The difference between the official rate and the parallel market selling rate is approximately ₦42.70 per dollar. Exchange rates fluctuate depending on dollar supply, demand, market liquidity and trading activities. The parallel market rate may also vary across locations and individual currency dealers. Nigerians seeking foreign exchange for international travel, school fees, business transactions and other payments are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks and licensed Bureau De Change operators before completing transactions.
