items.title: N50,000 relief fund: FG explains how beneficiaries will be selected
items.description: The Federal Government, FG has outlined how selected poor and vulnerable Nigerian households can receive a ₦50,000 cash grant under its National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI). The programme, implemented by the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, is designed to help vulnerable households cope with rising living costs through direct cash transfers into mobile wallets. According to the programme’s guidelines, beneficiaries will receive the money through designated payment providers, including ALAT, MoMo, NairaGram, OPay and Moniepoint. The government said the intervention uses mobile wallets to ensure that financial support reaches beneficiaries quickly and transparently, with independent checks conducted during each payment cycle. How to receive the FG’s ₦50,000 cash grant The government outlined four steps for selected beneficiaries to access the payment. 1. Receive an SMS notification Selected beneficiaries will receive a text message from one of the designated payment providers informing them that they have been selected for the programme. 2. Confirm participation Recipients are required to reply YES to the message to indicate their consent to participate in the programme. The guidelines state that no payment will be made without the beneficiary’s consent. 3. Activate the mobile wallet Following confirmation, a mobile wallet will be opened and linked to the beneficiary’s phone number and National Identification Number (NIN). 4. Receive and withdraw the money The sum of ₦50,000 will be credited to the beneficiary’s wallet. Recipients can withdraw the money through a Point of Sale (POS) agent, at a bank or spend directly from their mobile wallets. USSD codes to withdraw the ₦50,000 grant Beneficiaries will receive additional SMS instructions from their respective payment providers after their wallets have been credited. The government provided the following withdrawal codes: ALAT (Wema Bank): Dial 94523#. MoMo PSB: Dial 6710#. NairaGram: Dial 72600#. OPay: Dial 95520# or use the mobile application. Moniepoint: Dial 557327# or use the mobile application. How beneficiaries are selected According to the programme’s guidelines, beneficiaries are selected using verified national identity records and the National Social Register. The selection process is designed to identify poor and vulnerable households eligible for the intervention. The government explained that individuals cannot apply independently or pay to be included in the beneficiary list. It also clarified that not everyone will be included in the first group of beneficiaries. FG warns Nigerians against fraud The government cautioned beneficiaries against fraudsters who may attempt to exploit the cash transfer programme by demanding money or personal banking information. It said the programme is free and that nobody is authorised to request payment to facilitate the release of the ₦50,000 grant. The guidelines listed three ways beneficiaries can identify genuine programme messages: Messages must come from ALAT, MoMo, NairaGram, OPay or Moniepoint. Recipients will only be asked to reply YES or dial their payment provider’s designated USSD code. Messages will never request payment, a Personal Identification Number (PIN), a One-Time Password (OTP) or require recipients to click a link. The government also warned beneficiaries against sharing their PINs, OTPs or passwords with anyone, including agents and officials. It advised recipients to ignore messages from unauthorised senders and contact the programme’s helpline if they are unsure about the authenticity of a notification. Frequently asked questions about the NERSI ₦50,000 grant What is NERSI? The National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI) is a Federal Government relief programme designed to help Nigerian households cope with rising living costs. It is implemented by the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction. How much will beneficiaries receive? Each selected beneficiary will receive ₦50,000 in their mobile wallet. The government says the full amount will be credited without deductions. Is the ₦50,000 payment a loan? No. The payment is a Federal Government grant, not a loan, and beneficiaries are not required to repay it. Who is eligible for the cash transfer? Beneficiaries are selected from the National Social Register and verified national identity records. Individuals cannot apply or pay to be included in the list. Those selected will receive an SMS notification from their designated payment provider. Why was I selected, and how did the government obtain my phone number? According to the programme’s guidelines, beneficiaries are selected using information from the National Social Register and verified national identity records. Their phone numbers are obtained from these records and shared only with the relevant payment provider for the purpose of disbursing the grant. The government also stated that beneficiaries’ personal information would be used only for the programme. items.title: Lutte contre le financement du terrorisme au Burkina et au Sahel : des journalistes outillés sur de bonnes techniques d’investigation
items.description: La Cellule nationale de presse Norbert-Zongo (CENOZO) sur le journalisme d’investigation en Afrique de l’Ouest, en collaboration avec le Programme des Nations unies pour le développement (PNUD), a organisé du 27 au 30 octobre 2026 à Koudougou, un atelier de formation au profit des journalistes burkinabè sur les enquêtes relatives aux trafics illicites et au financement du terrorisme. Organisée dans le cadre du projet : « Edification d’une paix durable : appui au renforcement des capacités du Burkina Faso à comprendre, prévenir et contrer la menace du financement du terrorisme », cette formation de 30 journalistes burkinabè par la Cellule nationale de presse Norbert-Zongo (CENOZO), dans la cité du Cavalier rouge du 27 au 30 octobre 2026, a visé plusieurs objectifs. Il s’est agi d’une part, de renforcer leur compréhension sur les méthodes et mécanismes de financement du terrorisme au Burkina et au Sahel, de renforcer leurs compétences en méthodologie d’enquête sur les trafics illicites, leurs capacités en matière de cybersécurité et de protection des sources. D’autre part, de les doter de techniques, des outils de collecte et d’analyse de documents financiers. Pour le coordonnateur de la CENOZO, Arnaud Ouédraogo, cette formation était de donner des moyens aux journalistes, de mieux comprendre les économies illicites qui alimentent les groupes terroristes. « L’idée, c’est de leur permettre d’appréhender le phénomène, les mécanismes, de dénoncer, de sensibiliser les populations et de donner plus de lisibilité aux autorités, afin qu’elles prennent des mesures idoines pour renforcer la lutte », a-t-il justifié. Dans sa communication sur la méthodologie d’enquête sur les trafics illicites et le financement du terrorisme, il a insisté sur le choix du sujet, l’angle de traitement, la formulation d’hypothèses, la cartographie des sources et le plan d’investigation. Camarade Ouédraogo a également mis l’accent sur l’intérêt des Outils d’investigation en sources ouvertes (OSINT) qui permettent de géolocaliser certains phénomènes et d’exploiter des images satellitaires sans se déplacer dans les zones à risque. L’analyse des données financières, où les trouver quand le journaliste enquête sur les trafics illicites ? Ce volet a été décortiqué par la formatrice, Elza Sandrine Sawadogo. Elle a souligné que lorsqu’un journaliste d’investigation enquête sur une société, la question primordiale est de savoir : A qui appartient la société ? Qui est le propriétaire réel ? Qui a signé la facture ? « Nous pouvons trouver souvent ces informations dans les rapports financiers, parfois volumineux et rédigés en Anglais et il faudra que nous soyons vigilants », a-t-elle prévenu. Savoir aborder les sujets La typologie des cyberattaques, la sécurité du journaliste et des mots de passe, les traces numériques et la gestion des accès des applications, ont été développées par Ignace Sossou de la CENOZO. L’expert du PNUD, Losséni Cissé, qui a fait l’état des lieux des méthodes et mécanismes de financement des groupes terroristes au Burkina Faso et au Sahel, a signifié que l’une des principales causes du terrorisme est son financement, lequel financement, à son avis, vient le plus souvent de l’extorsion des fonds, des explosifs, des ressources naturels, notamment l’or, des rackets, rançons, enlèvements, du trafic des personnes, drogue, carburant, bétail et de médicaments. « Le terrorisme est un phénomène complexe et il faut savoir aborder les sujets. L’alternative pour nos pays, c’est la cohésion sociale. Les moyens efficaces de lutte, c’est la bancarisation », a-t-il convenu. Le représentant du gouverneur de la région de Nando, Blaise Zongo, a pour sa part, rappelé que la lutte contre le financement du terrorisme ne relève pas uniquement des services de sécurité et des autorités judiciaires, mais aussi des journalistes, qui, à travers leurs investigations, contribuent à mettre en lumière les réseaux crimi- nels, les circuits financiers illicites et les pratiques qui alimentent l’insécurité. Afsétou SAWADOGO

items.title: Egyapa Mercer demands parliamentary probe into Ghana-linked cocaine seizures
items.description: Former Sekondi MP Andrew Egyapa Mercer has called for a bipartisan parliamentary investigation into cocaine seizures linked to Ghana since January 2025, questioning how the consignments were able to leave the country and raising concerns about conflicting accounts of the latest interception in Lebanon. He has also given the government seven days to publish the roadmap of its anti-drug trafficking task force, which was expected to be released on October 1. Mr Mercer wants President John Dramani Mahama to engage Lebanese authorities and issue a joint statement clarifying whether the Beirut operation was a Ghana-led controlled delivery and when Ghanaian security agencies were first notified. The calls follow the arrest of a Syrian passenger at Rafic Hariri International Airport in Beirut, where Lebanese authorities reportedly seized 46.7 kilogrammes of cocaine from his luggage. Lebanese Customs has described the interception as the largest drug seizure in the airport’s history. Speaking on Citi FM on Wednesday, November 4, Mr Mercer said the explanation provided by Ghana’s Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) appeared to differ from the account attributed to Lebanese authorities. “Our demands are really simple. He should constitute a bipartisan parliamentary inquiry and hold public hearings into every Ghana-linked cocaine seizure recorded since January 2025, from Amsterdam to Beirut. We are also calling on him to publish the task force roadmap, which was due on October 1, within seven days,” he said. He added that the President should issue a joint statement with Lebanese authorities, including the country’s Internal Security Forces, to establish whether Ghana played a leading role in a controlled delivery operation and when local agencies became aware of the case. “If you listen to the narrative from the Lebanese authorities and you relate it to what NACOC is telling us, clearly there’s a disconnect,” he said. Mr Mercer also questioned the absence of announced arrests in Ghana days after the Beirut interception, particularly given reports that NACOC had knowledge of the suspect’s movements and whereabouts while he was in the country. He argued that if Ghanaian agencies had participated in a controlled delivery operation, they should also be able to identify people the suspect had interacted with locally. “Clearly, clearly we are being gaslighted,” he added.

items.title: INEC warns media against fake results, deepfakes
items.description: ….Urges journalists to prioritise verification over speed By Steve Oko The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has cautioned journalists against amplifying unverified election results, manipulated content and misinformation capable of undermining public confidence in the 2027 general elections. The Commission also disclosed that it was strengthening its technological infrastructure, cybersecurity and results management systems to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process ahead of the polls. Abia State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Prof. Sylvia Uchenna Agu, gave the warning on Wednesday at the 2026 Media Retreat and Press Week of the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Abia State Council, held at Bishop Nwedo Pastoral Centre, Umuahia. Speaking on the theme, “Safeguarding Electoral Integrity in the Digital Age: INEC and the Media Ahead of the 2027 General Elections,” Agu identified misinformation, disinformation, artificial intelligence-generated deepfakes, cloned voices and manipulated result sheets as emerging threats to electoral credibility. She urged media organisations to prioritise verification over speed, warning that the race to break news must not come at the expense of national stability and public trust. “The race to break the news must not break the nation,” the REC cautioned, stressing that journalists must resist the temptation to publish unverified information in pursuit of exclusives. She advised media practitioners to cross-check election-related information with INEC before broadcasting or publishing, noting that failure to verify claims could expose news organisations to credibility challenges. Agu also cautioned against declaring results based on information from unauthorised sources, urging journalists not to become channels for disseminating unverified results. She called on the media to support voter education by explaining relevant provisions of the Electoral Act, 2026, particularly those relating to voter accreditation, electronic transmission of results and transparency in the electoral process. The REC said the new legal framework had strengthened safeguards around elections, citing provisions mandating the use of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) for accreditation and electronic transmission of polling unit results to INEC’s Result Viewing Portal (IReV). She also highlighted provisions prescribing penalties for officials who deliberately frustrate the electronic transmission of results, adding that the law had strengthened transparency and accountability in the electoral process. On technological preparedness, Agu said INEC was building on lessons from previous elections to improve BVAS, IReV, the electronic EC8A and its Results Management System. She explained that the electronic EC8A system was designed to detect inconsistencies between manually completed polling unit result sheets and electronically captured results, with discrepancies preventing uploads until they were resolved. The REC recalled how BVAS helped expose an alleged manipulation of voter accreditation figures in a local government area of Abia State during the 2023 general elections. According to her, BVAS recorded 27,000 accredited voters in the affected local government area, but the figure was allegedly altered manually to 102,000, triggering controversy. “BVAS was the game changer in 2023. It checkmated frivolous accreditations. It was BVAS that saved the situation in Abia because, in a particular LGA, BVAS captured 27,000 as accredited voters, but it was handwritten as 102,000. “So, when the controversy came up, our ICT experts simply looked at the figure in IReV as captured by BVAS,” Agu said. She said the incident demonstrated the importance of technology in protecting electoral integrity and preventing discrepancies in accreditation figures from going undetected. The REC urged Nigerians to repose confidence in INEC, assuring them that the Commission was strengthening its systems and processes to deliver credible elections in 2027. She said the Commission was also enhancing cybersecurity, protecting election data, improving system monitoring and strengthening disaster recovery mechanisms to ensure the reliability of its digital infrastructure. Agu disclosed that INEC was exploring the responsible application of artificial intelligence to improve planning, data analysis and operational efficiency while maintaining human oversight and accountability. She, however, emphasised that technology alone could not guarantee credible elections without adequate training, testing, operational preparedness and collaboration among relevant departments and officials. The REC described the media as a critical constitutional partner in the electoral process, citing Section 22 of the 1999 Constitution, which mandates the press to hold government accountable. She urged journalists to balance their watchdog responsibilities with professional ethics, accuracy and responsible reporting, particularly during the sensitive election period. Agu said the Commission remained committed to collaborating with digital platforms to address demonstrably false electoral content while intensifying voter education through its official communication channels. She expressed confidence that credible elections in 2027 would depend on the collective commitment of INEC, the media and other stakeholders to transparency, professionalism and the national interest. The REC assured journalists of INEC’s continued openness to engagement, reiterating the Commission’s commitment to conducting free, fair, credible and inclusive elections. More than 30 media practitioners participated in the retreat organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of Abia NUJ as part of its efforts to deepen democracy and enhance journalistic efficiency. items.title: What the US midterms mean for ties with China
items.description: A sweeping victory for Democrats in US midterm elections this week, giving them control of Congress, presents both an opportunity and a challenge for top rival China, analysts say. Here is how the outcome of the vote, which offers the Democratic Party the power to stymie President Donald Trump’s maverick foreign policy, could impact the thorny relationship between Washington and Beijing: Will tariffs be limited? Winning control of both houses in the US Congress puts Democrats in a position to limit Trump’s liberal use of tariffs on Chinese products in the two years he has left in office, analysts say. That could be a blow to Trump, who had wielded duties throughout a frenzied US-China trade war before the two sides reached a truce, set to expire in January. If Democrats limit Trump, that means he “will be less able to leverage a tariff card in negotiations with China”, said Wu Xinbo, dean at the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai. However, Democrats will also have to weigh their actions against the popularity of Trump’s tariffs among US businesses. Congress will “take every opportunity to thwart (Trump’s policies) over the next two years”, said Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies at Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University. But Democrats will still have to tread carefully on further restricting tariffs that “are popular with unions, blue-collar workers and small businesses… who have historically been a base constituency for the Democrats”, Thompson said. Congress will be “less inclined to support measures that would sharply escalate pressure on China if doing so risks raising costs for American consumers and businesses or increasing the likelihood of conflict”, said Patricia Kim, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington. Taiwan a ‘game changer’? The issue of Taiwan, the US-backed democratic island claimed by Beijing, could be a “game changer”, said Neil Shearing, group chief economist at Capital Economics. Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer and has sold billions of dollars’ worth of arms to Taiwan that the island would use to fend off a potential Chinese attack. But Trump threw the US stance into question in May when he declared that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip in talks with China. His administration has since delayed for months a $14-billion batch of weapons. China could use the remaining two years of Trump’s presidency to increase pressure on Taiwan, particularly if Beijing “judges that Washington is distracted or that Trump would be willing to agree terms to not intervene”, Shearing wrote in a note. Trump, who recently hailed his “great friendship” with China’s President Xi Jinping, has so far resisted political pressure from Democrats — and some Republican lawmakers — to greenlight the arms package. But a Democrat-controlled Congress “may force Trump to resume arms sales to Taiwan next year”, Wu said. “If that happens, that will also undermine the stability of US-China relationship.” Alternatively, for China, renewed support of Taipei from the US Congress may be “a stronger incentive for (Beijing) to play it safer with Taiwan”, said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute. Nevertheless, Thompson pointed out, while Congress can pass bills requiring Trump to approve an arms sale, the president retains the power to veto it “or simply ignore it”. Will Beijing treat Trump as a lame duck? From China’s perspective, even though Trump has been politically weakened by the midterms, Beijing is unlikely to change its strategy towards working with him, analysts say. “Beijing is likely to continue cultivating him through high-profile, leader-to-leader engagement with Xi Jinping, viewing this as the least costly way to manage relations with Washington,” said Kim. “Neither Beijing nor Washington appears to expect or seek a fundamental improvement in bilateral relations,” she added. Tsang of the SOAS China Institute said “Trump being relegated to lame-duck status will be used by the Chinese to put more pressure on him”. But, he added, Beijing is “calculating” and “would not want to push too hard and trigger Trump behaving totally irresponsibly”.

items.title: SIAO 2026: le Mali et le Niger célébrés au nom de la fraternité sahélienne
items.description: La 18e édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO) a consacré, mercredi 4 novembre 2026, une journée spéciale au Mali et au Niger, pays invités spéciaux. Présidée par le secrétaire général du ministère de l’Industrie, du Commerce et de l’Artisanat, Alassane Ouédraogo, la cérémonie a été marquée par des prestations artistiques, des découvertes gastronomiques et des échanges de présents entre les délégations. La fraternité entre les peuples du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger s’est illustrée à l’occasion de cette journée dédiée aux deux pays invités spéciaux de la 18e édition du SIAO. La cérémonie a connu la participation de plusieurs personnalités diplomatiques, notamment des représentants des ambassades du Ghana et du Congo au Burkina Faso. Les festivités ont été animées par la troupe Imûhars du Niger et la troupe Bazani Théra du Mali, avec, en toile de fond, la dégustation de mets traditionnels des deux pays. Représentant le ministre chargé de l’Artisanat, Serge Gnaniodem Poda, le secrétaire général du département, Alassane Ouédraogo, a salué la présence des délégations malienne et nigérienne. Pour lui, cette participation témoigne de l’excellence des relations diplomatiques, économiques, culturelles et fraternelles entre les trois pays membres de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel (AES). « Notre ambition doit être de faire émerger un véritable espace de coopération artisanale au sein de l’AES, dans lequel nos artisans pourront davantage travailler ensemble, valoriser leurs complémentarités et conquérir collectivement les marchés », a-t-il souhaité. Il a également appelé à traduire la fraternité entre les trois pays en réalisations concrètes, au bénéfice de leurs populations. Prenant la parole au nom des autorités maliennes, l’ambassadeur du Mali au Burkina Faso, Issouf Oumar Maïga, a souligné la portée stratégique de cette rencontre. Il a présenté l’AES comme un projet d’intégration socio-économique et un espace de souveraineté et d’interdépendance. Selon lui, les salons artisanaux des trois pays, notamment le Salon international de l’artisanat du Mali (SIAMA), le Salon international de l’artisanat pour la femme (SAFEM) du Niger et le SIAO, sont appelés à se compléter pour constituer une véritable plateforme sous régionale de promotion des savoir-faire. Evoquant le thème de cette édition, il a insisté sur la nécessité d’articuler artisanat traditionnel, transformation locale et industrialisation. Il a, par ailleurs, plaidé pour un meilleur accès au financement des jeunes créateurs et des femmes artisanes, ainsi que pour la promotion de la commande publique en faveur des produits locaux. Au nom des autorités nigériennes, la chargée d’affaires de l’ambassade du Niger au Burkina Faso, Salifou Koubra, a exprimé sa reconnaissance au pays hôte pour cette distinction et l’accueil réservé à sa délégation. Elle a indiqué que le Niger participe à cette édition avec 200 artistes et 54 stands, une mobilisation qui traduit sa volonté de faire connaître la diversité de son patrimoine artisanal. Adama SAWADOGO

items.title: Une reconnaissance aux lourdes conséquences
items.description: Dans la Corne de l’Afrique, les initiatives diplomatiques sont rarement anodines. La présentation des lettres de créance de Michael Lotem comme ambassadeur d’Israël au Somaliland, au Président Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, à Hargeisa, ainsi que la pose de la première pierre d’une future ambassade israélienne, marquent une nouvelle étape dans le rapprochement entre les deux parties. Au-delà du caractère historique de cet événement pour les autorités du Somaliland, cette initiative ouvre une nouvelle séquence de tensions diplomatiques et géopolitiques dans une région déjà traversée par de profondes rivalités. Pour comprendre les enjeux de cette décision, il faut remonter à 1991, année au cours de laquelle, le Somaliland a proclamé son indépendance à la suite de l’effondrement de l’Etat somalien. Depuis lors, ce territoire fonctionne avec ses propres institutions, dispose d’une administration, organise des élections et exerce un contrôle sur une grande partie de son territoire. Pourtant, malgré plus de trois décennies d’autonomie de fait, il n’a jamais bénéficié d’une reconnaissance internationale significative. La Somalie continue de le considérer comme une partie intégrante de son territoire national. Dans ce contexte, la décision israélienne constitue une rupture diplomatique majeure et une victoire symbolique pour les autorités de Hargeisa, qui cherchent depuis longtemps à sortir de leur isolement international. Cependant, cette avancée ne saurait être analysée sous le seul prisme de la reconnaissance de l’autodétermination. Situé sur les rives du golfe d’Aden, à proximité du détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, le Somaliland occupe une position de premier plan sur l’une des principales voies maritimes reliant la mer Rouge à l’océan Indien. Ce passage constitue un axe vital pour le commerce international, notamment pour le transport des hydrocarbures et des marchandises entre l’Asie, l’Europe et le reste du monde. Dès lors, l’intérêt d’Israël pour ce territoire dépasse manifestement le simple cadre des relations diplomatiques bilatérales. Les autorités somaliennes voient dans cette reconnaissance une atteinte directe à leur souveraineté et à leur intégrité territoriale. Le Président Hassan Sheikh Mohamud soupçonne Israël de rechercher des avantages militaires et stratégiques dans cette partie de la Corne de l’Afrique. Au-delà du face-à-face entre Mogadiscio et Hargeisa, les conséquences pourraient également se faire sentir dans les relations entre les différents acteurs régionaux. Quant aux autres Etats de la région, ils pourraient être amenés à prendre position face à une initiative qui remet indirectement sur la table la question sensible des frontières héritées de l’histoire. Par ailleurs, cette évolution intervient dans un contexte sécuritaire particulièrement préoccupant. En effet, la reprise des affrontements au Yémen entre les rebelles houthis et les forces gouvernementales, conjuguée aux menaces qui pèsent sur la navigation en mer Rouge, rend la zone de Bab el-Mandeb encore plus sensible. Dans ces conditions, une présence israélienne renforcée à proximité de ce passage maritime sera être perçue par certains acteurs régionaux comme une tentative d’étendre l’influence de Tel-Aviv dans une zone stratégique. En outre, cette reconnaissance place les organisations régionales, notamment l’Union africaine, devant un véritable dilemme diplomatique. L’organisation continentale demeure attachée au principe de respect de l’intégrité territoriale des Etats et à la stabilité des frontières héritées de la décolonisation. C’est pourquoi, la prudence devrait prévaloir face à une question qui dépasse largement les ambitions diplomatiques d’Israël et les aspirations internationales du Somaliland. Toutefois, la construction d’une légitimité internationale ne saurait se faire au prix d’une déstabilisation durable de l’environnement régional. Cela dit, la nomination d’un ambassadeur israélien au Somaliland constitue un signal géopolitique susceptible de rebattre les cartes dans la Corne de l’Afrique et de renforcer les rivalités autour de la mer Rouge. Il appartient donc aux acteurs régionaux et internationaux de privilégier le dialogue plutôt que les démonstrations de force. Car, dans cette partie du continent, où les conflits sont déjà nombreux, une nouvelle ligne de fracture pourrait transformer un rapprochement bilatéral en une crise aux conséquences imprévisibles pour toute la région. Soumaïla BONKOUNGOU

items.title: 2027: APC flags off Enugu campaign in Nsukka, vows to deliver Mbah, Tinubu, other candidates
items.description: …Governor highlights projects, promises more roads, jobs, infrastructure …Charges electorate to sweep away opposition with their votes The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Enugu State on Wednesday officially flagged off its campaign for the 2027 general elections, with party leaders and stakeholders pledging to mobilise voters across the state for the re-election of Governor Peter Mbah and President Bola Tinubu. The campaign flag-off, which held at Nsukka Township Stadium, witnessed a large turnout of party faithful, political office holders, traditional and community leaders, as well as supporters from across the three senatorial districts. Speakers at the event described the mammoth crowd as a demonstration of the APC’s political strength in Enugu State, insisting that the party was determined to consolidate its presence and secure victory for all its candidates in the forthcoming elections. Addressing the gathering, Governor Mbah highlighted his administration’s investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, economic development, and revival of moribund assets and completion of abandoned projects. He urged the people to assess his government’s performance through its achievements and ongoing projects, noting that the opposition had not even presented any manifesto. Reflecting on his journey to Nsukka ahead of the rally, Mbah said the ongoing dualisation of the Penoks–T-Junction – Ugwogo-Opi-Nsukka road had significantly reduced travel time and improved safety. “I left the office a few minutes past 1pm. It took me two to three minutes to get to T-Junction from Penoks. And it just reminded me of how motorists could have spent so much time, sometimes up to 30 minutes or hours if we did not dualise that road. “From T-Junction all the way to Nsukka, I noticed that work was going on right left, green, what have you. The contractor assured me that a realistic commissioning date is before the end of this year. “Another thing the road reminds me is that we have kissed empty Mondays goodbye. Once upon a time, we dreaded traveling on that road because of fear of attack are gone. Today, we have kissed it goodbye,” he stated. According to him, the administration’s infrastructure programme is not merely about constructing roads, but also about reconnecting communities, expanding economic opportunities and promoting greater integration across the state. He cited the 40km Owo-Ubahu-Amankanu-Umualor-Ikem virgin dual carriageway, which connects to Obollo-Afor road as another intervention designed to improve connectivity, and now links communities in the northern part of the state, while also serving as a new gateway to the North Central part of the country. On education, Mbah said the Smart Green Schools initiative was fundamentally designed to transform the quality of learning and prepare children for a productive future and modern economy. He disclosed that the government had recruited more than additional 6,000 teachers, who were undergoing training at the state’s Centre for Experiential Learning and Innovation, as part of the efforts to move education in the state away from the traditional emphasis on memorisation and repetition towards critical thinking, creativity, innovation and problem-solving. In the healthcare sector, the governor said his administration was constructing Type-2 Primary Healthcare Centres across the state’s 260 electoral wards, with each facility provided with healthcare personnel and accommodation, including a two-bedroom residential unit. On economic development, Mbah listed the reopening and operations of the Presidential Hotel, International Conference Centre, United Farm Products Limited, Songhai Enugu Integrated Farm and Sunrise Rice Flour Mill, among other investments, as evidence of the state’s efforts to stimulate economic activities and create employment opportunities. He also described Enugu Air as more than an airline, saying it represented the state’s readiness to attract investment, tourism and business opportunities. “Enugu Air represents more than an airline to us. It is our statement that we are open for business and we are open for tourism. We are open for people to come here and live. “So, in a few weeks, Enugu Air will have a direct flight to London. Before the end of the first quarter next year, we will also have a flight to the United States and China,” he enthused. The Governor, however, acknowledged that more work remained to be done, particularly in road infrastructure, reiterating his administration’s commitment to its 10,000-kilometre road construction target. “We are not measured by our words; we are measured by our results. We don’t say things that we don’t deliver on. What we commit to, we deliver,” he said. The governor also highlighted his administration’s efforts to clear inherited pension and gratuity liabilities, disclosing that the state had approved N32 billion and started paying gratuity arrears dating back to year 2000. He also acknowledged the role of President Tinubu’s economic reforms in creating additional fiscal opportunities for state governments, which he said his administration had leveraged to invest in infrastructure, social services and employment generation. The governor further commended the President for federal interventions in the South-East, particularly the establishment of the South East Development Commission, approval of regional gas pipeline projects, road infrastructure and appointments of indigenes of the zone into key positions. He specifically referenced the appointment of an indigene of Nsukka as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Nigeria, saying the development addressed a long-standing aspiration of the university’s host community. Earlier, Deputy Governor Ifeanyi Ossai said the forthcoming elections presented an opportunity for the people to sustain the development programmes of the current administration and accused the opposition of disinformation. The Director-General of the Enugu APC Campaign Council, Chief Charlie Mbah; elder statesman and former Governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, represented by the Commissioner for Local Government Matters, Deacon Okey Ogbodo; APC Deputy National Chairman (South), Dr. Ben Nwoye, who represented the party’s National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda; Enugu State APC Chairman, Dr. Martin Chukwunwike; Senator Osita Ngwu, representing Enugu West Senatorial District; Senator Ikeje Asogwa of Enugu North Senatorial Zone; Minister of Innovation , Science and Technology, Dr. Kingsley Udeh, SAN; Secretary to Enugu State Government, Prof. Chidiebere Onyia; Member representing Nkanu West/Nkanu East Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Nnolim Nnaji; Member representing Igboeze North/Udenu Federal Constituency; South East Zonal Woman Leader of the APC, Dr. Oby Ajih; Speaker of the Enugu State House of Assembly, Hon. Uche Ugwu; and Chairman of Nsukka Local Government Area, Engr. Jude Asogwa, reiterated Tinubu and Mbah’s outstanding performance, expressing confidence that all APC candidates would succeed at the polls/ Meanwhile, with the official flag-off, the Enugu State APC said it was set to commence a statewide campaign tour, taking its message to nooks and crannies of the state. The post 2027: APC flags off Enugu campaign in Nsukka, vows to deliver Mbah, Tinubu, other candidates appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ecole nationale des postes : la 51e promotion apte à servir la Nation
items.description: 82 stagiaires composant de la 51e promotion de l’Ecole nationale des postes (ENAPOSTE) ont effectué leur sortie, mercredi 04 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Après une année académique de cours théoriques et pratiques, cumulés avec des stages en milieu professionnel, les stagiaires de la 51e promotion de l’Ecole nationale des postes (ENAPOSTE) sont désormais aptes à servir à travers la Poste Burkina Faso. Leur sortie officielle a eu lieu, le mercredi 4 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, en présence du secrétaire général du ministère de la Transition digitale, des Postes et des Communications électroniques, représentant la ministre Aminata Zerbo. Composés de 18 contrôleurs, 10 agents d’exploitation et 54 agents de bureau, la promotion s’engage à relever les défis pour maintenir la Poste Burkina Faso parmi les entreprises prospères, résolument tournées vers l’innovation. La déléguée de la promotion, Nelly Bambara, a, au nom de ses camarades réaffirmé leur disponibilité, ainsi que leur ferme détermination à mettre les compétences acquises au service du secteur postal. Selon elle, la formation des stagiaires qui a été axée sur la qualité du service postal ne repose pas uniquement sur la maîtrise des procédures et des outils techniques mais exige également l’écoute attentive des clients, la rigueur dans l’exécution des tâches, le respect des délais, la courtoisie et la confidentialité… « Nous allons faire de ses valeurs les principes de notre conduite professionnelle, afin de contribuer, chacun à son niveau, à l’amélioration continue de la qualité des services rendus aux usagers, au renforcement de leur confiance et au rayonnement de la Poste Burkina Faso », a-t-elle promis. Un taux de réussite de 100% Au cours de la cérémonie, les stagiaires sont rentrés en possession de leur diplôme. Les trois meilleurs dans les trois filières de formations ont chacun reçu des kits témoignant de leur mérite. Avec un taux de réussite de 100%, la directrice générale de l’ENAPOSTE, Koumbo Rahja Barry, a expliqué qu’un tel exploit témoigne de l’engagement des apprenants, de la qualité de l’encadrement pédagogique et de la rigueur des enseignements dispensés. Elle a souligné que dans les trois filières dispensées, les majors de promotion, ont obtenu 18,93 de moyenne pour les agents de bureau, 18,35 pour les contrôleurs et 18,26 pour les agents d’exploitation. Elle a rappelé que cette année académique a été marquée par l’organisation de cours théoriques, de travaux pratiques et de mise en situation professionnelle, de stages d’immersion dans les structures opérationnelles de la Poste Burkina Faso. La directrice générale a ajouté qu’une attention particulière a été accordée à la maîtrise des opérations postales et financières, à la relation client, à l’utilisation de l’outil numérique, ainsi qu’aux exigences d’éthique et de déontologie et à la qualité de service. Elle a, en outre, expliqué qu’au-delà des résultats académiques, leur ambition demeure de former des professionnels immédiatement opérationnels, capables de s’adapter aux mutations du secteur postal et de contribuer efficacement à la transformation de la Poste Burkina Faso. S’adressant à la promotion, Koumbo Rahja Barry l’a invitée à respecter les procédures, à cultiver l’esprit d’équipe et à faire preuve de discrétion dans le traitement des informations, tout en demeurant attentifs aux besoins des clients. Yassimine Aminata OUARMA

items.title: Le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou Sana, à propos de l’expulsion des orpailleurs de la Guinée : « Les autorités burkinabè n’ont pas été informées à l’avance de cette opération »
items.description: Le ministre de la sécurité, Mahamadou Sana, a conduit, le mercredi 4 novembre 2026, une délégation gouvernementale à Bamako pour s’enquérir de l’état des orpailleurs burkinabè expulsés de la Guinee et organiser leur retour au Burkina Faso. Nous vous proposons l’intégralité de son message à l’issue de sa rencontre avec les autorités maliennes. C’est suite à la situation au niveau de la frontière Mali-Guinée, où vous avez suivi depuis 72 heures, nos compatriotes qui ont été refoulés. Alors, nous avons été mandatés par les camarades, le Président du Faso et le Premier ministre, de venir non seulement évaluer la situation et d’identifier aussi les différents problèmes, et aussi d’apporter l’assistance nécessaire à nos compatriotes. Mais aussi de voir dans quelles mesures organiser de façon digne et décente le rapatriement de nos compatriotes. Dès notre arrivée, nous avons bénéficié de l’hospitalité légendaire de nos homologues frères du Mali, et nous avons pu tenir une rencontre pour évaluer réellement la situation existentielle. Alors, ce qui a été évoqué, c’est que des mesures ont été déjà prises par nos frères du Mali, en termes d’accompagnement et d’assistance humanitaire. Toute chose qui a permis aussi de soulager nos compatriotes. En plus de cela, l’ambassade du Burkina Faso au Mali a pu apporter une assistance nécessaire, tant au niveau de Bamako qu’au niveau de la zone frontalière, pour pouvoir aussi soulager nos compatriotes. Donc, ensemble, nous avons réfléchi sur la meilleure stratégie pour, non Les autorités maliennes et burkinabè ont échangé pour une meilleure prise en charge des ressortissants burkinabè. seulement renforcer cet accompagnement et cette assistance humanitaire, mais également voir dans quelles mesures, à partir de demain, dans les meilleurs délais en tout cas, de pouvoir ramener nos compatriotes au Burkina Faso. Alors, il faut souligner qu’au niveau central, nous avons déjà pris des mesures nécessaires. Une centaine de bus a été déjà mobilisés, dont 50 sont déjà en route sur le territoire malien, pour qu’aujourd’hui nous puissions organiser ce rapatriement. Aussi, à partir du Burkina Faso, des sites d’accueil ont déjà été identifiés. Il y aura également le retour de ces compatriotes dans leurs familles respectives. Il faut souligner que cette opération, malheureusement, est déplorable et regrettable. Parce qu’on se dit qu’une telle opération ne peut quand même pas être déclenchée sans une planification. Et qui parle de planification, parle aussi d’évaluation des conséquences et des implications. En aucun cas, ni les autorités maliennes, ni les autorités burkinabè n’ont été informées à l’avance de cette opération. Toute chose qui n’a pas permis d’anticiper également sur ce qui se passe actuellement. Deuxièmement, de ce qui nous remonte, en tout cas, nous avons enregistré des blessés. Même parfois des blessés par balles. Ce qui laisse croire que nos compatriotes ont subi des traitements cruels, inhumains et dégradants. En tant que pays frère, c’est réellement regrettable. Il était nécessaire de souligner cela. C’est l’occasion pour moi, une fois de plus, de réitérer tout le témoignage des plus hautes autorités du Burkina Faso à l’adresse des autorités maliennes et au peuple malien pour toute l’assistance qu’ils ont pu apporter à nos compatriotes pour que jusque-là, en tout cas, ils puissent être soulagés. Propos retranscris par la Rédaction

items.title: Flash
items.description: Le Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), en ce moment, bat son plein à Ouagadougou. Cet espace dédié à l’artisanat africain attire inévitablement de nombreuses personnes. Pour cette édition 2026, ce sont plus de 6 000 exposants qui sont présents avec environ 800 000 visiteurs. Mais, dans une foule, il y a toujours de mauvais éléments. Si certaines personnes sont présentes sur le site avec une bonne foi, d’autres le sont à d’autres fins. Les pickpockets, les voleurs, les bandits et les escrocs utilisent des techniques de diversion et de discrétion pour dérober des biens dans les lieux publics. C’est pourquoi, malgré le dispositif sécuritaire déployé sur les différents sites, les visiteurs sont invités à rester vigilants et à se rendre sur les lieux avec le strict minimum. Garder les sacs fermés, placés devant soi et surveiller les poches dans les zones à fort passage. Les téléphones font partie des objets les plus convoités et doivent faire l'objet d'une vigilance constante. Galedie Kétoura SIMPORE

items.title: Un coup de massue
items.description: Les temps changent sur le théâtre des opérations au Burkina Faso. Ceux qui, hier encore, semaient la terreur, imposaient leur loi aux populations et circulaient en maîtres dans certaines localités, ont du plomb dans l’aile aujourd’hui. Les Forces combattantes sont désormais à leurs trousses et ne leur laissent aucun répit. La récente opération dans la forêt de Konga, qui a coûté la vie à Saïdou Diallo, alias Djabiri Mangan le Borgne, et à plusieurs de ses acolytes, en est une éclatante illustration. Ce 29 octobre 2026 restera comme une journée particulièrement difficile pour les criminels du Groupe de soutien à l’islam et aux musulmans (GSIM). En s’attaquant à leur dispositif dans cette zone du Sourou, les éléments des Forces spéciales antiterroristes de campagne (FORSATEC) ont fait preuve d’une remarquable efficacité opérationnelle. Mieux, ils ont réussi à mettre hors d’état de nuire un hors la loi qui constituait un maillon important de l’organisation terroriste dans le Sourou et le Yatenga. Adjoint du chef de la base terroriste de Konga/Gomboro et acteur central de la logistique criminelle, Djabiri Mangan le Borgne n’était pas un simple exécutant. Il participait à l’approvisionnement des criminels en tenues et accessoires militaires et assurait l’écoulement du bétail arraché aux populations. Sa neutralisation représente donc bien davantage qu’une victoire symbolique. C’est une partie de la machine criminelle qui vient d’être sérieusement grippée. Il faut saluer le courage, l’abnégation et le professionnalisme de nos Forces combattantes. Face à un ennemi qui connaît parfaitement les zones qu’il écume et qui se nourrit de la peur des populations, nos soldats font preuve d’une détermination remarquable. Leur capacité à débusquer les responsables terroristes jusque dans leurs repaires, à démanteler leurs bases et à récupérer leurs moyens logistiques témoigne des efforts accomplis dans la conduite des opérations. Les résultats enregistrés ces derniers mois confortent cette montée en puissance de nos braves forces combattantes. Le 25 juillet 2026, 15 terroristes, dont leur chef Sangaré Barry Manga, avaient été neutralisés dans la forêt de Kinséré, dans la province de la Kossi. Le 16 janvier dernier, 57 autres avaient été renvoyés à l’au-delà lors d’une embuscade entre Koogo et Menè, dans le Koulpélogo. Parmi eux figurait Karim Torodo, alias Abdoul Bachirou, présenté comme l’émir du GSIM pour le Nakambé. Ces coups de massue successifs portés aux responsables terroristes envoient un message sans équivoque : aucun sanctuaire ne saurait constituer un refuge permanent pour les ennemis de la paix. Les criminels ne peuvent éternellement se cacher derrière les forêts, les grottes ou les zones difficiles d’accès pour échapper à la détermination des Forces combattantes. Le temps de l’impunité doit céder définitivement la place à celui de la reconquête. Mais ces victoires ne doivent rien au hasard. Elles sont le fruit de l’engagement des hommes sur le terrain, de leur préparation, de leur courage et, surtout, de leur professionnalisme. Derrière chaque opération réussie, il y a des combattants qui affrontent le danger, souvent au péril de leur vie, pour que des millions de Burkinabè puissent espérer retrouver une existence normale. A ces hommes et à ces femmes, la Nation doit reconnaissance et soutien. Certes, le chemin vers la victoire définitive reste exigeant. Les groupes terroristes peuvent tenter de se réorganiser et de reconstituer leurs réseaux. Mais une chose est désormais essentielle : les Forces combattantes ne subissent plus passivement la menace. Elles frappent, traquent et désorganisent l’adversaire. Cette capacité à prendre l’initiative constitue un atout majeur dans cette guerre de longue haleine. Au-delà des bilans militaires, l’enjeu est de faire reculer durablement la peur, de libérer les populations de l’emprise des criminels et de restaurer l’autorité de l’Etat dans chaque portion du territoire national. A Konga, nos Forces combattantes viennent de rappeler une vérité : le Burkina Faso n’a pas renoncé à sa liberté et à sa souveraineté. Aux ennemis de la patrie, le message est clair : le peuple burkinabè, debout derrière ses défenseurs, ne se résignera jamais à vivre sous le joug de la barbarie. La patrie se défend, la souveraineté se conquiert et la victoire se construit avec des hommes déterminés. Hommage à nos Forces combattantes ! Kamélé FAYAMA

items.title: APC has mechanism to manage our govs, Rainbow Coalition’s feud — Yilwatda
items.description: *We’ve no plan to make Nigeria one party state *Nigerians should choose leaders based on records, character, capacity to deliver *Says Tinubu’s reforms must translate into jobs, food, better incomes, security By Soni Daniel, Northern Regional Editor National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, has said the ruling party has no ambition to turn Nigeria into a one-party state despite the influx of politicians from opposition parties into its fold. Yilwatda, who spoke on the 2027 general elections, governance and the APC’s preparations for the polls, said a strong ruling party and a competitive multiparty democracy could coexist. In an interview with Vanguard, the APC chairman also said the party had mechanisms to resolve differences between some APC governors and the Federal Capital Territory Minister, Nyesom Wike’s Rainbow Coalition, insisting that internal disagreements would not derail its preparations for the elections. He defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the administration had established measures to reposition the economy but must now translate them into jobs, affordable food, better incomes and improved security. Yilwatda urged Nigerians to assess candidates on their records, character and capacity to deliver rather than allow political differences to dictate their choices. As a democrat, are you not worried that the mass exodus of other politicians into the ruling APC can create a one-party state if the APC wins in January next year? I am a democrat, and I believe that Nigeria’s democracy is stronger when political parties are vibrant, competitive and able to offer citizens credible alternatives. The APC does not seek to eliminate opposition, nor do we believe that a healthy democracy can be sustained without it. The movement of politicians from one party to another is a feature of democratic politics. Individuals make such decisions for different reasons, and every Nigerian has the constitutional right to freedom of association. What matters is that these movements are voluntary and conducted in accordance with the law. However, the responsibility for maintaining a competitive political environment does not rest with the APC alone. Opposition parties must also strengthen their internal structures, build public confidence, articulate credible policies and organise effectively. Our ambition is not to turn Nigeria into a one-party state. Our ambition is to build a party that Nigerians freely choose because of its leadership, programmes and record of performance. A strong APC and a competitive multiparty democracy are not mutually exclusive. We will continue to respect the rights of other parties to organise, campaign and seek the people’s mandate. How is the APC under your leadership helping to actualise the dream of progressive politics, which seeks to make life better for all and reduce authoritarianism? Progressive politics must ultimately be measured by its impact on the lives of ordinary citizens. It is not enough to speak about progressive ideals; we must demonstrate them through policies, institutions and programmes that expand opportunities, protect citizens’ rights and improve living standards. Under my leadership, the APC is focused on strengthening internal democracy, promoting responsible leadership, expanding grassroots participation and ensuring that the party remains connected to the needs and aspirations of Nigerians. Our structures must provide opportunities for women, young people, professionals and people from different communities to participate meaningfully in political decision-making. We also recognise that the party has a responsibility beyond winning elections. We must provide constructive feedback to the government, communicate its policies honestly and ensure that the concerns of Nigerians reach the appropriate authorities. Progressive politics also demands respect for the Constitution, the rule of law, freedom of expression and the independence of democratic institutions. These principles are essential to building a society where government serves the people and power is exercised responsibly. Ultimately, our objective is to ensure that the Renewed Hope Agenda translates into tangible improvements in people’s lives. For the APC, progressive politics must mean better opportunities, greater inclusion, stronger institutions and a government that remains accountable to the people. The progressive ideology of the APC drives the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Tinubu, which seeks to improve the economy and tackle insecurity, among others. As the chairman of the party, to what extent do you think these ideals have been actualised since 2023? The Renewed Hope Agenda represents a broad programme of economic reform, infrastructure development, social investment, improved security and sustainable national development. Since 2023, the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has undertaken significant reforms intended to address longstanding structural challenges in the Nigerian economy. These include the removal of the petrol subsidy, foreign-exchange reforms, tax reforms, efforts to improve government revenue, investments in infrastructure and measures to support vulnerable households and productive sectors of the economy. As the governing party, our responsibility is to assess progress honestly, defend policies that are producing results and encourage improvements wherever implementation falls short of expectations. My assessment is that the administration has established a reform direction and undertaken important measures to reposition the economy. The next critical task is to accelerate the translation of those measures into jobs, affordable food, better incomes, improved security and stronger public services. The Renewed Hope Agenda should be judged not only by the reforms initiated, but increasingly by the measurable improvements Nigerians experience in their daily lives. That is the standard we must continue to pursue. One of the cardinal goals of this administration is poverty reduction. Do you think the administration has succeeded in reducing poverty in Nigeria? Poverty reduction is one of the most important tests of any government’s performance, because the ultimate purpose of economic growth is to improve human welfare. The administration has introduced and pursued interventions intended to cushion the effects of economic adjustment, support vulnerable households, expand access to education and credit, promote agriculture and small businesses, and create opportunities for employment and enterprise. These measures are important because poverty cannot be sustainably reduced through cash assistance alone; it also requires productive jobs, stronger businesses, better education and access to essential services. Our position as a party is that the government’s efforts must be judged by evidence of their reach, effectiveness and impact. Social interventions must get to the intended beneficiaries, agricultural production must improve, businesses must be able to grow, and workers must experience meaningful improvements in their purchasing power. We therefore recognise the progress being pursued while acknowledging that much more remains to be done. Poverty reduction is a continuing national responsibility, not a task that can be completed overnight. Our objective must be to move Nigerians beyond survival towards economic security, productive employment and a genuine opportunity to improve their standard of living. How are you going to manage the conflict between some APC governors and the FCT Minister’s Rainbow Coalition in their efforts to win support for the President? The overriding objective of every APC stakeholder should be the success of President Tinubu and the party in the 2027 elections. That objective requires cooperation, mutual respect and effective coordination among governors, ministers, party leaders, elected representatives and grassroots organisations. Where differences arise between individual stakeholders or mobilisation groups, our responsibility as party leadership is to provide a platform for dialogue and reconciliation. We will encourage all parties to focus on the common objective rather than allow differences over structures, influence or methods of mobilisation to become sources of division. At the same time, we must recognise that political mobilisation can take different forms. Groups may emerge around particular constituencies, interests or initiatives, but their activities should complement the party’s established structures rather than create unnecessary rivalry. The APChas established organs and procedures for managing internal disagreements. We intend to use those mechanisms to promote consultation, clarify responsibilities and ensure that our collective campaign effort is properly coordinated. I would not want to characterise every difference of opinion as a crisis. What matters is how we manage those differences and whether all stakeholders remain committed to the party’s objectives. Our approach is dialogue, reconciliation and coordination. No personal or group interest should be allowed to outweigh the collective interest of the APC and the national objective of delivering good governance. Are you worried about the division? As National Chairman, I take every concern about unity within the party seriously. The APC is a large political organisation with governors, ministers, legislators, party executives and millions of members across the country. With such diversity, differences of opinion are inevitable. What matters is that we do not allow those differences to become permanent divisions. We have established party structures, leadership channels and reconciliation mechanisms to address grievances and resolve disagreements in a constructive manner. I am encouraged by the fact that our members share a common objective: to strengthen the party, support the Renewed Hope Agenda and prepare effectively for the 2027 elections. That common purpose provides a strong foundation for resolving whatever differences may arise. We are also conscious that Nigerians expect political leaders to demonstrate maturity, restraint and a willingness to work together. We must not allow individual disagreements to distract us from the responsibility of serving the people. I remain confident in our ability to manage our differences through consultation and responsible leadership. Unity does not mean that everyone must agree on everything. It means that, despite our differences, we remain committed to a common purpose and respect the procedures that bind us together. What advice do you give to Mr. President and Nigerians as we prepare for the 2027 polls? My advice to President Tinubu is to remain focused on governance, sustain the reform agenda, intensify efforts to improve security and ensure that the benefits of economic recovery reach Nigerians across all social groups and geographical regions. Above all, we must remember that our political differences do not diminish our shared identity as Nigerians. No election is worth the loss of innocent lives, the destruction of property or the weakening of our national unity. My message to Nigerians is simple: let us make 2027 a contest of ideas, records and credible plans for the future, not a contest of bitterness or violence. The ultimate winner must be Nigeria and the Nigerian people. How satisfied is your party with the programmes and timelines released by INEC for the coming elections? The APC respects the constitutional mandate and operational independence of the Independent National Electoral Commission. INEC is responsible for organising elections in accordance with the Constitution and the Electoral Act, and we expect it to discharge that responsibility professionally, impartially and transparently. As a political party, we have a legitimate interest in the electoral timetable, because it guides our preparations, candidate selection processes, campaign activities and mobilisation of voters. We therefore study the commission’s guidelines carefully and engage through the appropriate institutional channels whenever clarification or a legitimate concern arises. Our expectation is that the timetable should provide sufficient clarity for political parties, candidates and voters to prepare effectively, while allowing INEC to meet its legal obligations. Equally important is the timely publication of guidelines, transparent procedures, credible voter registration and accreditation processes, and the effective deployment of technology where appropriate. We believe that confidence in elections depends not only on the timetable but also on how consistently the rules are applied to all political parties. The APC will comply with the applicable electoral laws and INEC guidelines, and we expect every other political party to do the same. Our interest is not merely in having elections conducted on schedule, but in having a process that is credible, transparent, peaceful and capable of earning the confidence of Nigerians. How do you respond to the criticism that the APC-led government has caused more hardship than bringing renewed hope to Nigerians since coming to power in 2023? The administration inherited longstanding economic and structural challenges, but it would not be responsible to suggest that this fact alone removes its obligation to address the difficulties Nigerians face today. President Tinubu’s administration has undertaken difficult reforms intended to stabilise the economy, improve public revenue, address distortions and create the conditions for sustainable growth. These reforms are intended to produce long-term benefits. Our responsibility as the governing party is to explain the rationale for these policies while ensuring that the government remains responsive to their consequences. Economic reform must be accompanied by effective social protection, increased domestic production, improved infrastructure, job creation and measures that help households cope with rising living costs. We must also ensure that public resources are used responsibly and that relief programmes reach the people for whom they are intended. I would not claim that everything has been achieved or that every Nigerian is already experiencing the benefits of the reforms. There is still important work to be done, and the government must continue to improve implementation and delivery. However, we believe that the reforms provide a foundation for a more resilient economy, and we will continue to support measures that deliver measurable improvements in the lives of Nigerians. Renewed Hope must be more than a slogan. It must become a daily experience reflected in affordable food, better incomes, secure communities, reliable infrastructure and expanding opportunities for ordinary Nigerians. That is the outcome we are working towards, and that is the standard by which we must be judged. items.title: Économie russe : face aux pénuries de main-d’œuvre, le Kremlin se tourne vers les travailleurs étrangers
items.description: La semaine dernière, le ministère russe du Travail et de la Protection sociale a proposé un projet de résolution fixant à 382 800 le nombre de permis de travail octroyés l’an prochain aux ressortissants de pays soumis à une obligation de visa Квота на визовых работников в 2027 году в РФ может составить 382,8 тыс. человек », Interfax , 30 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Il s'agit du plus haut niveau depuis 2015. En 2021, avant le lancement de l’invasion à grande échelle de l’Ukraine, ce chiffre était de 102 000 permis. Ce projet de résolution, qui doit encore être adopté par le gouvernement – habituellement fin novembre ou début décembre –, concerne surtout des travailleurs en provenance de Chine, d’Inde, du Vietnam, du Turkménistan, du Bangladesh, du Sri Lanka et de Turquie. Selon le ministère russe du Travail, « l’autorisation d’embaucher des travailleurs de pays soumis à visa n’est délivrée qu’après confirmation par une commission interministérielle régionale que l’entreprise ne parvient pas à trouver d’employés au sein de la région ». Ces derniers pourraient être amenés à travailler sur d’importants projets d’infrastructure, comme la construction de complexes gaziers dans la région de l’Amour, la deuxième phase du cosmodrome de Vostotchny ou la ligne à grande vitesse Moscou-Saint-Pétersbourg. Certains pourraient également être affectés à la zone économique spéciale de production industrielle d’Alabouga, créée en 2005 dans la république du Tatarstan, à quelque 900 kilomètres à l’est de Moscou. C’est à Alabouga que sont assemblés la majeure partie des drones d’attaque à longue portée de type Shahed utilisés par l’armée russe pour frapper l’Ukraine. Selon le CSIS, les travailleurs étrangers constituent l’un des trois principaux groupes de travailleurs à Alabouga, aux côtés des jeunes Russes, recrutés dès l’âge de 15 ans par le collège polytechnique de la zone, et des ouvriers nord-coréens Human rights abuses in drone production at Yelabuga , CSIS et George W. Bush Institute, 14 octobre 2026.'> 2 . Dans le cadre du programme Alabuga Start (« Алабуга Старт »), des jeunes femmes âgées de 16 à 22 ans, principalement originaires de pays du Sud, notamment d’Afrique, se voient promettre des emplois dans l’hôtellerie et la restauration par des recruteurs sur les réseaux sociaux. Une fois arrivées en Russie, la plupart sont affectées à la production de drones. Leurs billets d’avion, leur logement et leurs cours de russe sont déduits de leur salaire, et leurs passeports sont confisqués. Les pertes de l’armée russe sur le front ukrainien ont atteint un niveau record en octobre. Depuis 2022, Moscou aurait perdu entre 1,4 et 2,1 millions d’hommes, tués ou blessés, dont 374 000 à 770 000 morts, soit 0,6 % à 1,2 % de la population masculine du pays d’après les estimations des Nations unies. Ces pertes pèsent lourdement sur l’économie, déjà confrontée à une pénurie de main-d’œuvre qualifiée. Si la crise du marché du travail n’a pas commencé en février 2022, la guerre a accéléré une dégradation structurelle déjà engagée, et, selon Alexandra Prokopenko, en a figé les effets pour plusieurs décennies. L’article Économie russe : face aux pénuries de main-d’œuvre, le Kremlin se tourne vers les travailleurs étrangers est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: ORC moves to strike off 453 companies, dissolves 323 others
items.description: The Office of the Registrar of Companies (ORC) has announced plans to remove 453 companies from Ghana’s Companies Register, while confirming the dissolution of another 323 entities whose names have already been struck off. The two separate notices, issued under the Companies Act, 2019 (Act 992), affect a total of 776 companies and form part of the statutory process for updating the national register of registered businesses. In a press release dated November 4, 2026, the ORC said the 453 companies were subject to strike-off proceedings under Section 289(3) of the Act, while the remaining 323 had been struck off following the expiration of the prescribed notice period and now stood dissolved under Section 289(5). Three-month notice for 453 companies The Registrar said the names of the 453 companies were published in Volume 48 of the ORC Companies Bulletin on October 15, 2026. Under Section 289(3), the companies will be struck off the register at the end of three months from the date of the notice, unless cause is shown to the contrary. The process means the affected companies have a statutory period within which any grounds against their removal must be brought forward before the strike-off takes effect. 323 companies already dissolved In a separate development, the ORC confirmed that 323 companies had been removed from the register after the notice period provided under Section 289(5) elapsed without cause being shown against their removal. The Registrar said the intention to strike off the companies had earlier been published in Volume 40 of the ORC Companies Bulletin. Following the expiration of the period specified in that notice, the companies were struck off the register. Their dissolution was subsequently published in Volume 49 of the bulletin, dated October 15, 2026. The ORC said the companies therefore stood dissolved in accordance with Section 289(5) of Act 992. The Registrar’s notice was addressed to corporate entities, creditors, shareholders, members of the public and other relevant stakeholders. The two actions distinguish between companies still undergoing the strike-off process and those whose removal has been completed and dissolution confirmed.

items.title: ‘How BVN exposed fake Amnesty beneficiaries’
items.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA—The Presidential Amnesty Programme, PAP, has said its insistence on the Federal Government’s Bank Verification Number, BVN, policy has exposed fake beneficiaries and fraudsters feeding off the programme. The office, while condemning what it described as blackmail and campaign of calumny against its administrator, Dr. Dennis Otuaro, by some misguided elements from the Niger Delta, said it would not succumb to blackmail and will not sideline the BVN policy designed to link all bank accounts belonging to individuals and eradicate corruption. “The PAP office cannot be the exception in the execution of the government’s policy on BVN designed to eradicate corruption in the society,” the Office said in a statement, yesterday, Mr. Igoniko Oduma, Special Assistant on Media to the Administrator, said. “Clearly, anybody using the tool of blackmail to arm-twist the office to sideline BVN is either a criminal or a fraudster, who should be under security watch. The Office has asked them to come for verification of their claims, but they will not. “These serial blackmailers are purveyors of falsehood and hollow narratives; they are driven by sheer greed with the sole objective of denting Dr. Otuaro’s image and distracting him from focusing on the task given to him by President Bola Tinubu. “These misguided elements are angry with Dr. Otuaro for prudent management of resources, and introducing reforms that have sanitised the PAP. Many of them are angered by what is statutorily paid to them by the Office. Some want to be awarded bogus contracts which, the office under Otuaro, is not inclined to do.” The programme said rather than divert funds to satisfy blackmailers, resources are being deployed efficiently for lasting peace and security in the Niger Delta, with tangible results including 13,300 onshore and over 500 offshore scholarships, distribution of laptops to beneficiaries, and prompt payment of ex-agitators’ monthly stipends. It listed other achievements as employment of four cadet pilots and 20 aviation trainees after training, on-the-job training for 40 cadets, professional certification for 98 maritime cadets, and training of over 360 stakeholders on alternative dispute resolution and mediation. items.title: Interior Minister visits injured GIS Officer at 37 Military Hospital following Hamile explosion
items.description: The Minister for the Interior, Alhaji Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, has visited the 37 Military Hospital in Accra to assess the condition of a Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) officer critically injured in an explosion at Hamile in the Upper West Region. The officer, airlifted to Accra for specialised medical care, is currently receiving treatment at the hospital, an official statement signed for the Head/Public Affairs Department of GIS by DSI Barbara Sam, the Deputy Head/Public Affairs Department, said. During the visit, Alhaji Muntaka expressed sympathy to the officer’s family and assured them of the Government’s full support throughout the recovery process. He further assured the family that all medical expenses arising from the incident would be covered and that every effort would be made to ensure the officer receives the best possible care. The Minister also cautioned the public against the unsafe handling, transportation, and use of explosives. He urged citizens to comply strictly with the laws and safety regulations governing the possession, movement, and use of explosive materials, warning that negligence could have devastating consequences for individuals and communities. The Deputy Comptroller-General of Immigration in charge of Command Posts and Operations (DCG/OPS), Faisal Disu, who led a delegation of senior Immigration officers to accompany the Minister, briefed him on the circumstances surrounding the incident. According to DCG Disu, a four-member Immigration patrol team on routine duty encountered a tricycle carrying two occupants travelling towards Burkina Faso through an unapproved route. When the team attempted to stop the tricycle, the rider veered off the road, prompting the officers to pursue them. It was later established that the occupants were transporting explosives, which detonated during the incident, resulting in casualties. The incident led to the death of one Immigration officer and two civilians on the tricycle at the scene, while one other immigration officer sustained severe injuries and was airlifted to Accra and admitted to the 37 Military Hospital for specialised care. The hospital has assured the Service of its commitment to providing the injured officer with the highest standard of medical attention. DCG Disu further disclosed that, following the explosion, some youth in the area attacked Ghana Immigration Service installations, reportedly in reaction to the patrol team’s actions. He, however, stressed that the officers were carrying out their lawful mandate to prevent cross-border crime and other illegal activities along the country’s borders. This has resulted in a curfew being imposed on the Hamile Township in order to forestall further attacks on Immigration Officers during the night. In a related development, the Regional Security Council, including the Immigration Service, met with chiefs and the Hamile-Happa Traditional Area Committee to dialogue on the concerns raised. The ongoing engagement has helped calm tensions in Hamile and its environs. The Ghana Immigration Service reaffirms its unwavering commitment to safeguarding Ghana’s territorial integrity and combating cross-border crime. The Service also appeals to border communities to cooperate with security agencies and refrain from attacking officers or public installations, particularly when personnel are performing their lawful duties. The Service extends its deepest condolences to the family of the deceased officer and wishes the injured officers a speedy and full recovery.
