items.title: CHOGM: King Charles describes slave trade as shameful chapter of history
items.description: King Charles III of the United Kingdom and Head of the Commonwealth has described the slave trade as a shameful chapter of human history. He described the slave trade as a “shameful chapter of history” that “fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow.” Speaking at the opening of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, he acknowledged the enduring shadow of the transatlantic slave trade and urged Commonwealth member nations to draw lessons from history. “We cannot change the actions of those who came before us. We can, however, learn from the past.” The King said. He noted that the transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over the islands and other Members of their Commonwealth. “As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow.” It would be recalled that on March 25, 2026, the United Nations General Assembly adopted a landmark resolution (Resolution A/RES/80/250/A/80/L.48) declaring the transatlantic trade in enslaved Africans and racialised chattel enslavement as “the gravest crime against humanity”. Spearheaded by Ghana’s President John Dramani Mahama and backed by the African Union and the Caribbean Community (CARICOM), the resolution passed with 123 countries voting in favour. “The more I have furthered my own understanding of the issues, through listening, learning and looking, the more committed I have become to finding ways for us to work in modern partnership to address the wrongs of the past with action for the future,” King Charles noted. He said through improving access to education, investing in jobs and opportunities, encouraging intra-Commonwealth trade, and inspiring vital climate resilience measures across the world; saying, “I have always felt that there is so much that can be done to help lift up those who struggle against hardship and disadvantage”. The Monarch said the Commonwealth of today was not merely a product of the past, but a response to the world of today. He said brutal conflict stalked their world, destroying lives and casting long shadows across the globe. Touching on the theme of this year’s CHOGM – “Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth”, the King said it represented such a vital opportunity for them all. He said to realise these opportunities, in the field of climate and nature, for example, transformative investment could drive real change, such as in renewable energy and resilient infrastructure, in sustainable, regenerative agriculture and agroforestry and food systems, in their oceans, forests and in the natural systems upon which their economies and societies ultimately depend. He said in the Caribbean, as in so many parts of their Commonwealth, climate change was not some distant prospect; it was an alarming reality. He said as they know, large Ocean States had contributed little to the causes of climate change, and yet they were among those bearing the greatest cost. “If we mobilise climate finance through the private sector, and with the leveraging capacity of the public sector, we can drive investment into climate resilience,” he stated. The King noted that nature herself was an essential form of capital that sustains our prosperity and wellbeing, and yet they had persisted for too long to live off Nature’s capital rather than her income. The King commended Madam Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey, the Secretary-General of the Commonwealth, for announcing a series of Nature and climate proposals for consideration at this year’s Heads Meeting: a new Commonwealth Nature Initiative with funding to restore habitats; work with insurers on the proposal for a Commonwealth-backed mutual insurance mechanism to provide rapid payouts after disasters; and aspirations for a Commonwealth Net Zero Fund to provide access to credit for a renewable-energy revolution. The Monarch said Commonwealth leaders, the private sector and civil society would work together on innovative proposals in support of all the citizens of the Commonwealth, especially in countries most vulnerable to the reality of climate change. This year’s meeting, which is on the theme “Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth”, is being attended by President John Dramani Mahama. The Commonwealth, which is headed by King Charles III of the United Kingdom, is a voluntary association of 56 independent and equal countries. It is home to 2.7 billion people and includes both advanced economies and developing countries. Thirty-three members of the Commonwealth are small states, including many island nations.

items.title: State Police: Kano, Cross River, Abia, Niger, Benue, Oyo yet to approve bill; gets Nov 19 deadline
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA—THERE are strong indications that the National Assembly is prepared to transmit the State Police Bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent as thirty states have so far approved the bill. The proposed State Police system has crossed a major constitutional hurdle, with 30 State Houses of Assembly approving the amendment required to pave the way for its establishment. This leaves six states yet to submit approved bill to the National Assembly for onward transmission to the President for subsequent assent. The six states that have not approved the bill are Kano, Cross River, Abia, Niger, Benue and Oyo. The Senate has, however, given them up till November 15 to do so, warning that failure to respond by the deadline could be deemed as withholding approval. The six states are expected to communicate their decisions before November 15, when the National Assembly intends to forward the proposed constitutional amendment to President Bola Tinubu for subsequent. Disclosing these while updating lawmakers on the progress of consultations with the 36 state legislatures on the proposed amendment yesterday, the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central, said the number of approvals had exceeded the constitutionally required two-thirds of the 36 state legislatures. According to him, for the process to be rounded off, it has to be in three phases, with the National Assembly expected to pass the bill; the approval by at least two-thirds of the state legislature; and the President to sign the bill into law. He added that the National Assembly had fulfilled its responsibility by passing the bill and transmitting it to all 36 State Houses of Assembly for consideration and approval. Bamidele said: “Let me explain again, for the avoidance of doubt, three keywords are used in the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, as amended. The first word is passage, the second word is approval and the third assent. “The reason the writers of our Constitution, our forefathers, put all these specific words is to ensure that no part of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria can be easily amended without the buying in of all the critical stakeholders at all levels of governance. “The passage of the bill was the responsibility of the National Assembly, and that has been completed. Approval is required from at least two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly in the country, while assent must subsequently be given by the President to complete the constitutional amendment process.’’ He explained that the constitutional requirements were deliberately designed to ensure that amendments to the nation’s supreme law enjoyed the participation and agreement of critical stakeholders across the different levels of government. Bamidele stressed that the 30 approvals already received were significantly above the constitutional requirement of 24 states, describing the development as evidence of widespread support for the proposed reform. “Two important points need to be emphasised. First, we needed the approval of at least two-thirds of the states for this constitutional amendment to proceed. “Two things that need to be emphasised here is that we needed two-thirds of the states at the very least for this to pass, and already two-thirds will be 24. So, as of yet, we already got 30 states, showing the popularity of this bill among Nigerians through the elected representatives in the State Houses of Assembly,” he said. The 30 states that have approved the proposal are Adamawa, Akwa Ibom, Anambra, Bauchi, Bayelsa, Borno, Delta, Ebonyi, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Gombe, Imo, Jigawa, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Kogi, Kwara, Lagos, Nasarawa, Ogun, Ondo, Osun, Plateau, Rivers, Sokoto, Taraba, Yobe and Zamfara. With 24 approvals required, the 30 states have already taken the proposal beyond the constitutional threshold. However, Bamidele said the National Assembly was still expecting formal responses from the remaining states. items.title: Voter register: INEC to purge 1.5m irregular registrants
items.description: •Amupitan can’t supervise credible polls in 2027 — Ezekwesili By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, is set to delete about 1.5 million voter registrations found to be irregular from the national register, ahead of the 2027 general elections. This is even as former Education Minister, Oby Ezekwesili, said yesterday that Nigeria could not conduct a credible 2027 election under an Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, led by Prof. Joash Amupitan. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this while receiving a delegation on a courtesy visit to the commission’s headquarters in Abuja yesterday. The delegation was led by the Special Representative of the United Nations Secretary-General for West Africa and the Sahel and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel, UNOWAS, Mr. Leonardo Santos Simão. Amupitan said technology-enabled verification helped the commission isolate the affected entries. The deletions, he explained, were part of a comprehensive cleaning of the register through the claims and objections process. The final register is scheduled for publication on December 15, 2026. Amupitan said the commission had registered approximately 103 million voters, with young Nigerians, aged 18 to 34, making up nearly 29 per cent of them. Amupitan said INEC would continue to strengthen the use of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, for accreditation, and the INEC Result Viewing Portal, IreV, for public access to polling-unit results. He said the commission was also planning a mock accreditation and election to test these tools, identify possible challenges and build public confidence before the 2027 polls. Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation and foreign information manipulation as major threats to electoral integrity. He warned that the growing misuse of Artificial Intelligence, AI, and coordinated online campaigns could undermine public confidence in the electoral system. INEC under Amupitan can’t supervise credible polls in 2027, says Ezekwesili Meanwhile, former Education Minister, Oby Ezekwesili, has said Nigeria cannot conduct a credible 2027 election under an Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, led by Prof. Joash Amupitan. According to her, INEC has lost all credibility to be an independent umpire of Nigeria’s elections. Oby, who spoke against the backdrop of allegations of corruption involving the voter register through the use of artificial intelligence, noted that INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, on October 30, 2026, told Nigerians that INEC registration officers purportedly used their official login credentials to inject AI-generated photographs, duplicate records and other fabricated entries into the preliminary register of voters. Ezekwesili said: “Let us be clear about what this is. This is not a hack from outside. This is not a glitch. This is sabotage from within the very institution to which the Nigerian people entrusted the register of our sovereignty.” ‘’The people paid to protect the list of citizens manufactured phantom citizens. The 2027 general elections are now a matter of months away, and the foundational document of those elections has been admitted by its custodian to be compromised. “I speak today as an Occupant of the Office of the Citizen, which I have long told the world, especially Nigerians, that it is the highest office in any democracy. ‘’It is the office from which all other offices, including that of the president, senators, governors, lawmakers and public appointees like the Chairman of INEC, derive their authority and legitimacy. ‘’The register of voters neither belongs to INEC nor the federal government nor the ruling party. It belongs to us, the citizens of Nigeria. Period! INEC merely holds it in trust. That trust, by its own admission, has been totally broken with the AI infiltration of the voter register.’’ She argued that INEC could not investigate itself, adding that “no institution that has just confessed to corrupting a national asset from within can then ask the nation to trust it alone to repair the damage. It is a principle of accountability so basic that we apply it to everyday contexts. ‘’The accused does not sit as judge. The staff who held the credentials, the supervisors who approved their access, the ICT department that built the platform with the loophole they exploited, and the commission that certified the display of that register all now have an interest in the size of this scandal being declared small. “Consider what INEC has done since the discovery. Its statement of October 27 named no cause. Three days later, its Director of ICT said on air that officers were compromised in several states, yet he also said he is still gathering evidence before reporting to the commission. “Almost one week after that, Nigerians still do not know how many records are affected, which states, which local governments, which officers, or whether a single one of them has been suspended, let alone handed to the police.” Vanguard News The post Voter register: INEC to purge 1.5m irregular registrants appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lutte contre le diabète : la prévention au cœur de la riposte
items.description: À l’occasion du lancement de sa campagne nationale de sensibilisation et de lutte contre le diabète, organisé hier mercredi 4 novembre 2026 au siège de l’Association des journalistes en santé, population et développement (Ajspd), l’Association sénégalaise de soutien aux diabétiques (Assad) a réuni plusieurs acteurs du secteur sanitaire autour des enjeux de cette maladie. Entre prévention, dépistage précoce, accès aux traitements et éducation thérapeutique, les intervenants ont insisté sur la nécessité de renforcer la mobilisation face à un problème de santé publique aux conséquences médicales, sociales et économiques importantes. Le diabète ne se combat pas uniquement dans les structures de soins. Sa prévention commence bien en amont, dans les habitudes alimentaires, l'activité physique et la capacité des populations à identifier les facteurs de risque. C'est l'un des principaux messages développés par le professeur Abdoulaye Lèye, endocrinologue-diabétologue, lors d’une rencontre organisée par l'Association sénégalaise de soutien aux diabétiques (Assad). Dans son intervention consacrée à l'état des lieux du diabète au Sénégal, aux complications et aux défis de la prise en charge, le Pr Lèye a insisté sur l'importance de la prévention primaire. La lutte contre les facteurs de risque passe, entre autres, par la prévention de l'obésité, la réduction de la sédentarité et l'adoption d'une alimentation équilibrée. Des habitudes qui, prévenues tôt, peuvent contribuer à réduire les risques de développer la maladie. Le spécialiste a également évoqué les possibilités offertes par certaines approches thérapeutiques. Les traitements médicamenteux et la chirurgie métabolique peuvent, chez certains patients, permettre d'obtenir une rémission du diabète et une amélioration des paramètres métaboliques. Ces résultats restent toutefois liés à un suivi médical rigoureux. Pour l'endocrinologue, la sensibilisation doit également évoluer dans son approche. Plutôt que de concentrer les messages sur les seules complications du diabète, il estime nécessaire de donner davantage de place aux moyens de les prévenir. L'éducation thérapeutique constitue, à ses yeux, un levier essentiel pour aider les patients à connaître leur maladie, à comprendre les enjeux de leur traitement et à améliorer leur équilibre glycémique. Cette bataille de l'information concerne aussi les médias. Le professeur Abdoulaye Lèye a rappelé leur rôle, aux côtés des professionnels de santé, dans la diffusion des connaissances. Mais les informations disponibles doivent être adaptées aux réalités sociales et aux conditions de vie des populations pour produire des changements concrets dans les comportements. Du côté des pouvoirs publics, la stratégie repose également sur le renforcement de la prévention et l'amélioration de l'accès aux soins. Directeur de la lutte contre Survenue de la maladie au ministère de la Santé et de l'Hygiène publique, Dr Moustapha Diop a assuré que le diabète figure parmi les priorités des autorités sanitaires. Classé parmi les maladies à soins coûteux, le diabète représente une charge importante pour les patients et le système de santé. Dans ce contexte, Dr Diop a insisté sur la nécessité de miser davantage sur la prévention. Il a notamment rappelé l'importance de la subvention de l'insuline, qui a contribué au maillage national de l'offre de soins. Le dispositif de prise en charge s'appuie notamment sur 27 centres intégrés et des cliniques dédiées au diabète. Un réseau que les autorités entendent consolider, tout en accordant une attention particulière au dépistage précoce. Il a également plaidé pour l'installation d'une véritable culture du bilan de santé au sein de la population. Au-delà des dispositifs médicaux et des politiques publiques, la lutte contre le diabète appelle ainsi une mobilisation qui implique les professionnels de santé, les associations de patients, les médias et les populations elles-mêmes. À travers sa campagne nationale de novembre 2026, l'Assad entend contribuer à cet effort collectif, en plaçant la sensibilisation, la prévention et le dépistage au centre des préoccupations. items.title: Farmer found dead with gunshot wound in Assin Ketukrom
items.description: Police have launched an investigation into the death of a 56-year-old farmer whose body was discovered in a room at Assin Ketukrom in the Assin North District of the Central Region, with a suspected gunshot wound to the abdomen. The deceased, identified as Kofi Sackey, was found lying on his back with a single-barrelled gun resting on his stomach on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Although the circumstances point to a suspected suicide, investigators are working to establish what happened before his death. A police report said the case was brought to the attention of the Assin Praso District Police Command at about noon by the deceased’s younger brother, Kofi Ansah. Mr Ansah reportedly told the police that he had returned from the farm at about 11:15 a.m. when he found his elder brother lying in a pool of blood in his room. A team of officers led by the District Commander, Superintendent Eric Yao Avudzivi, subsequently visited the house. They found the body in the middle of the room, with what appeared to be a deep gunshot wound to the abdomen, slightly above the navel. The firearm was found resting on the body. Information gathered by the police suggested that the incident occurred shortly before the body was discovered. A nephew, Acquah Emmanuel, told investigators that he had been watching television with other family members when Mr Sackey walked out of the room at about 11 a.m. A few minutes later, they heard a sound resembling a gunshot. The family members reportedly went outside to establish what had happened but found no one. It was only after Mr Ansah returned from the farm that the deceased was found in the room. The police documented the scene, took photographs and conveyed the body to the New Edubiase Government Hospital mortuary for preservation and autopsy. Police investigations are continuing to establish the circumstances surrounding the death and verify the accounts given by witnesses.

items.title: Flamingos beat Brazil to reach first U17 Women World Cup final
items.description: Nigeria’s U17 women’s team, the Flamingos, have reached the final of the FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup for the first time in history after defeating Brazil 3-1 in the semi-final. The Flamingos secured the historic victory with goals from Queen Joseph and Awawu Bashiru, who scored twice. Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute before Bashiru extended Nigeria’s lead in the 71st minute. Bashiru completed her brace in the 80th minute to seal Nigeria’s 3-1 victory and book their place in the final. The achievement marks a major milestone for the Nigerian side, who won bronze at the 2022 edition of the competition. The Flamingos will now face Japan in the final as they seek to win their first-ever FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup title. items.title: Tiaret, futur bassin de production de la pomme en Algérie
items.description: Après les Aurès, c’est au tour de la région de Tiaret d’attirer les investisseurs dans le domaine de la culture de la pomme . Les conditions climatiques et le prix élevé de ce fruit ont fini par convaincre de nombreux opérateurs à investir dans cette filière. C’est le cas d’Amine Derrar, dont les pommiers ont bel et bien commencé à donner une bonne récolte, 18 mois seulement après le début de l’opération de plantation. « Nous avons commencé en juin 2025 et vous voyez les bons résultats. Nous travaillons en respectant le processus technique, nous avons des ingénieurs et un réseau d’irrigation de goutte à goutte. Et nous suivons de près les nouveautés dans le domaine agricole », a expliqué l’arboriculteur au ministre de l’Agriculture, Sid Ali Khaldi, venu visiter l’exploitation qui s’étale sur 28 hectares. Tiaret : des conditions climatiques idéales pour le pommier Comme dans les Aurès où la pomme est reine, cette région des hauts plateaux de l’Ouest du pays profite de conditions climatiques propices pour les pommiers. « Notre verger est situé à 1.000 mètres d'altitude, et cumule plus de 800 heures de froid par an, un seuil thermique indispensable pour lever la dormance des arbres et garantir une bonne floraison. Le froid et le soleil sont les conditions de la qualité », précise l'investisseur. En plus du climat, ces bons résultats ont été favorisés par la disponibilité des réseaux d’électricité et d’irrigation auxquels sont raccordées plus de 1.300 exploitations agricoles dans la wilaya, selon les responsables locaux. L’expérience de cet investisseur de Tiaret témoigne de l’intérêt que portent de plus en plus d’investisseurs à l’arboriculture. Le succès de la culture de la pomme dans la région des Aurès, notamment à Khenchela et Batna, a inspiré d’autres opérateurs. Et la production ne cesse d’augmenter ces dernières années. Selon les données de Faostat, l’Algérie a produit 591.700 tonnes de pommes en 2024. Les superficies récoltées sont estimées à près de 32.000 hectares, avec un rendement moyen de 18,6 tonnes par hectare. La production de la pomme en Algérie a réalisé une croissance de 27 % entre 2014 et 2024, d’après FAOStat. Les prix de la pomme, de bonne qualité, sur le marché algérien peuvent atteindre 1.000 dinars à Alger. L’article Tiaret, futur bassin de production de la pomme en Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Après les midterms, une fenêtre pour la relation transatlantique ?
items.description: Testez le Grand Continent . Les idées et les analyses qu’on ne trouve nulle part. Mais que vous verrez bientôt partout. Dans votre boîte mail à partir de 8 euros par mois Le résultat historique des élections de mi-mandat américaines ouvre une période complètement nouvelle pour la suite du second mandat de Donald Trump. Sur le plan domestique, le président américain se trouve désormais très affaibli par une défaite qui sonne avant tout comme un référendum contre sa personne, ses pratiques et son bilan. Les conséquences de l’élection sont durables : les nouveaux sénateurs sont élus pour six ans et siégeront jusqu’à la fin de la présidence de Donald Trump, mais aussi pendant tout le mandat présidentiel suivant. Les résultats des midterms sont aussi très importants pour l’Europe. Sur le plan institutionnel d’abord, les démocrates disposent désormais au Congrès des moyens de contrôler beaucoup plus étroitement l’action de Donald Trump, même si l’exécutif américain est moins encadré par la Constitution en matière extérieure et militaire que sur les sujets domestiques. Ensuite, plus fondamentalement et à long terme, l’élection est la démonstration de la résilience et de la vitalité de la démocratie américaine (déjà illustrée par le rôle des contre-pouvoirs depuis deux ans), à de très nombreux égards : la forte participation, la façon dont les élections se sont tenues sans violence ni perturbation, l’acceptation des résultats par le Président, la diversité et la nouveauté des profils des candidats élus (pas seulement pour le Congrès, mais aussi aux fonctions de gouverneurs, par exemple), l’incapacité des sommes considérables d’argent privé dépensées dans la campagne par des milliardaires comme Elon Musk ou Vivek Ramaswamy à peser sur les résultats. Enfin, cette nouvelle donne au Congrès offre des opportunités inédites à l’Europe, pour autant que celle-ci fasse des propositions novatrices, quitte à revisiter certaines de ses propres références, et change d’échelle pour répondre à l’ampleur des enjeux. Des garanties institutionnelles à construire Sur l’avenir de la relation transatlantique, c’est d’abord aux Américains, et à la nouvelle majorité au Congrès, qu’il revient de rétablir la confiance. Les Européens, comme tous les partenaires traditionnels des États-Unis, peuvent à juste titre douter de l’intérêt de resserrer les liens avec un pays qui a confié deux fois à Donald Trump les fonctions suprêmes. Certes, au regard de leur ampleur, les résultats pourraient laisser augurer la défaite de ses héritiers à la présidentielle, dans deux ans. Mais il ne peut être exclu que l’un d’eux, inspiré par ses méthodes et sa pratique du pouvoir, accède un jour à la Maison-Blanche. Les fractures américaines qui expliquent l’émergence politique de Donald Trump se sont développées sur plus d’une génération. Les réduire prendra plus d’un mandat présidentiel, comme l’a montré la présidence de Joe Biden. Le contexte nouveau issu des midterms, mais aussi les réflexions menées aux États-Unis sur le nécessaire renforcement des institutions pour prévenir l’autoritarisme, permettent cependant l’émergence de solutions et de garanties nouvelles pour les Européens et les partenaires des États-Unis. Prenons la politique commerciale, domaine dans lequel Donald Trump a fait plier l’Europe avec un accord très déséquilibré, sans précédent pour l’Union européenne : la Constitution en confie la compétence au Congrès. Les Européens, comme tous les partenaires traditionnels des États-Unis, peuvent à juste titre douter de l’intérêt de resserrer les liens avec un pays qui a confié deux fois à Donald Trump les fonctions suprêmes. Renaud Lassus Donald Trump a pu agir en s’appuyant sur des délégations de compétences en matière de droits de douane, conférées par des textes souvent anciens, pour certains sortis de l’oubli par Robert Lighthizer, son représentant au commerce lors de son premier mandat. Si la Cour suprême s’est récemment opposée au président américain sur la façon dont il mettait en œuvre ces délégations, elle n’a pas condamné leur usage en tant que tel. Lors de son premier mandat, le président avait déjà fait beaucoup de mal aux intérêts européens, en particulier français, en les activant, sans en outrepasser le cadre. Il devient aujourd’hui possible de traiter ces risques de façon structurelle pour l’avenir. Le Congrès peut modifier ces délégations pour contraindre l’exécutif à obtenir son accord avant d’instituer des mesures commerciales contre les alliés des États-Unis. Il existe d’ailleurs déjà un précédent. Avant de devenir secrétaire d’État, lorsqu’il était sénateur de Floride, Marco Rubio avait fait adopter une disposition interdisant au président américain de quitter l’OTAN sans l’approbation préalable du Congrès. Le Congrès va par ailleurs engager un travail institutionnel pour renforcer l’encadrement des pouvoirs de l’exécutif et prévenir les risques autoritaires à l’avenir. Un tel processus s’était brièvement engagé en 2021, après l’attaque contre le Capitole. Il reprendra sur un large champ : le droit de grâce du président, y compris envers lui-même, l’étendue et les limites de son autorité sur les agences fédérales indépendantes, l’obligation pour l’exécutif de mettre en œuvre les décisions budgétaires votées par le Congrès, son pouvoir de nomination, autant de domaines dans lesquels Donald Trump a cherché à s’affranchir des normes de la démocratie américaine. Dans un tel contexte, des propositions visant à encadrer l’exécutif pour garantir la prévisibilité, la qualité et la stabilité des relations avec les alliés des États-Unis trouveront un écho favorable au Congrès. Ce que les démocrates reprochent à l’Europe Si les premiers pas pour rétablir la confiance doivent venir des Américains, les Européens, pour leur part, ne doivent pas méconnaître la dégradation sensible de l’image qu’ont d’eux les démocrates. De nombreux responsables démocrates influents estiment en effet que l’Union s’est montrée beaucoup moins exigeante et critique envers Donald Trump qu’à l’égard de Joe Biden. Ils soulignent que lors de l’adoption du plus grand plan de lutte contre le changement climatique jamais voté aux États-Unis ( l’Inflation Reduction Act ), les pays européens, qui dénonçaient jusque-là l’inaction américaine, ont surtout réagi négativement, critiquant des dispositions unilatérales et protectionnistes, avant de se montrer bien plus discrets sur la politique climatique de Donald Trump. Ils avancent aussi que l’Union a refusé de s’engager avec Joe Biden dans des rapprochements en matière de politique industrielle, au motif que les propositions américaines n’étaient pas conformes au droit du commerce international, pour conclure ensuite à Turnberry avec Donald Trump un accord bilatéral très déséquilibré , pourtant ouvertement contraire aux principes de l’OMC. Au Congrès, et à la Maison-Blanche s’ils la reconquièrent dans deux ans, les démocrates placeront aussi la relation avec la Chine au centre de leur agenda avec l’Union, comme question stratégique essentielle, voire comme préalable au reste du dialogue. Sur ce point aussi, la déception à l’égard de l’Europe est profonde. Les démocrates n’ont pas compris pourquoi, pendant le mandat de Joe Biden, l’Union s’est tenue à distance de l’agenda politique et commercial américain à l’égard de la Chine. Tout en reconnaissant la responsabilité centrale des États-Unis dans la lourde erreur de jugement qui voulait que l’intégration de la Chine dans les échanges internationaux amène celle-ci à devenir plus démocratique à l’intérieur et moins nationaliste à l’extérieur, ils estiment que l’Union a refusé de partager ce diagnostic pour des raisons idéologiques, liées à son attachement à la libéralisation des échanges. De nombreux responsables démocrates estiment que l’Union s’est montrée beaucoup moins exigeante et critique envers Donald Trump qu’à l’égard de Joe Biden. Renaud Lassus Un dossier juridique en particulier, très peu connu en Europe, a beaucoup pesé dans cette prise de distance, d’autant qu’une grande partie des élites démocrates sont des juristes de formation : le soutien apporté par la Commission européenne, au nom de la défense du multilatéralisme, aux décisions de l’organe d’appel du système de règlement des différends de l’OMC, y compris lorsque celui-ci a refusé de considérer, dans un contentieux sur les subventions octroyées par la Chine, les compagnies publiques chinoises comme des organismes publics, au motif qu’elles n’exerçaient pas d’autorité gouvernementale, une interprétation qui ne figure pas dans les textes de l’OMC. Chine, climat : les terrains d’une coopération nouvelle Le durcissement en cours de l’Union face aux pratiques économiques, commerciales et monétaires de la Chine semble aujourd’hui ouvrir la voie à de nouvelles coopérations. Avec plus de dix ans de retard sur les États-Unis, les pays européens jusqu’ici les moins résolus à l’égard du mercantilisme chinois, comme l’Allemagne, semblent désormais estimer à leur tour que le niveau atteint par les subventions, les surcapacités de production, les stratégies de vente à perte des entreprises chinoises menacent directement la pérennité des industries et des activités économiques en Europe, le tissu social et productif et, in fine, la stabilité politique des démocraties. Par ailleurs, l’acceptation sociale et politique de la transition énergétique, déjà complexe et difficile, serait vouée à l’échec, en Europe comme en Amérique, si la lutte contre le changement climatique se traduisait au final par la domination de monopoles chinois, la disparition de secteurs économiques entiers, la dépendance à l’égard d’entreprises chinoises capables d’interrompre leurs livraisons à des fins de pression politique. Pour leur part, les démocrates vont chercher à reprendre leur stratégie de réindustrialisation au bénéfice des régions les moins favorisées, autour de vastes investissements en matière environnementale et climatique, pour améliorer les conditions de vie des classes populaires américaines, et répondre aux fragilités sociales et politiques qui ont nourri l’essor politique de Donald Trump. C’est donc notamment sur ces questions que pourrait se concentrer, dès à présent, la reprise de la coopération transatlantique. En matière climatique, les États-Unis et l’Union européenne n’avaient pas pu se mettre d’accord, à la fin du mandat de Joe Biden, sur un traitement commun des importations selon leur contenu en carbone, dans certains secteurs comme l’acier et l’aluminium. L’Union pourrait proposer de reprendre ces discussions. Plus largement, l’Union a institué un mécanisme d’ajustement carbone à la frontière. Aux États-Unis, des projets de loi déposés au Congrès, y compris avec le soutien de sénateurs républicains, portent la même vision ; bloqués par l’administration Trump, ils pourraient désormais avancer. Un travail fondateur de rapprochement pourrait être engagé. De façon plus ambitieuse encore, les États-Unis et l’Union européenne pourraient travailler conjointement à un projet d’union douanière, couvrant les produits les plus importants pour la transition énergétique (les véhicules électriques, les panneaux solaires, les batteries, etc.). Dans ces secteurs, les États-Unis et l’Europe mettraient en œuvre de façon coordonnée (en associant d’autres États qui souhaiteraient se joindre à eux) les mêmes instruments (droits antidumping, mesures antisubventions), à l’égard des pays tiers qui subventionnent massivement leurs productions nationales. Les Américains ont un intérêt essentiel à ce que l’économie européenne ne disparaisse pas sous la pression chinoise ; les Européens, eux, ont intérêt à ancrer leur résolution nouvelle à l’égard de la Chine dans des accords contractuels avec d’autres pays comme les États-Unis, car il n’est pas sûr qu’ils trouvent en eux-mêmes la fermeté suffisante pour faire face aux menaces chinoises. Cette union douanière permettrait de retrouver un levier de pression systémique à la hauteur des enjeux. Lever les obstacles, des deux côtés de l’Atlantique Les obstacles à un rapprochement transatlantique n’en restent pas moins considérables. Donald Trump reste au pouvoir pour deux ans. Il existe désormais un profond passif. Les incertitudes sont nombreuses des deux côtés de l’Atlantique. Il faut cependant distinguer les obstacles véritables des barrières mentales (et parfois d’un certain manque d’imagination) qui peuvent exister côté européen. Un argument souvent avancé en Europe veut ainsi que les Européens se tiennent à distance des États-Unis et de leur système politique, économique, social, fondamentalement imprévisible, instable, inégalitaire, dominé par l’influence de l’argent privé, travaillé par des pulsions violentes sur le plan interne et dans le rapport au monde. Ces appréciations sont justes et reposent sur des éléments incontestables. Mais elles ne traduisent qu’une partie de la réalité et de l’histoire américaines. Les élections viennent de montrer la résilience de la démocratie américaine. De plus, dans la situation actuelle de doutes et d’incertitudes, l’apparition de perspectives nouvelles et positives dans une démocratie, a fortiori aux États-Unis, présente un intérêt majeur pour toutes les autres. Les fractures démocratiques, en Europe comme en Amérique, reposent aussi sur des fondements sociaux, politiques, technologiques, culturels, territoriaux, en grande partie communs, qui appellent des réflexions et des réponses communes. Les Américains ont un intérêt essentiel à ce que l’économie européenne ne disparaisse pas sous la pression chinoise. Renaud Lassus En d’autres termes, les citoyens qui cherchent en Europe à renforcer leurs démocraties ont tout intérêt à entretenir et à développer leurs liens avec les Américains qui partagent leur vision, et à la traduire en propositions concrètes, surtout au moment où ceux-ci viennent de remporter une victoire aussi nette au Congrès. Beaucoup estimeront cependant en Europe que le Parti démocrate et les Américains ont d’autres priorités que l’Europe au moment où ils cherchent à sortir de la période Trump. Le contexte n’a pourtant jamais été aussi favorable, pour peu que les Européens comprennent la séquence américaine qui s’ouvre et parviennent à s’y inscrire. De nombreux démocrates considèrent ainsi que la démocratie américaine ne pourra pas régler seule certaines causes essentielles des fragilités qui l’affectent aujourd’hui, comme l’impact d’Internet et des réseaux sociaux sur le contrat démocratique et sur l’espace public, cette agora où s’échangent les idées en démocratie (les fausses nouvelles, les polarisations numériques, l’influence disproportionnée des propriétaires des réseaux sociaux, les manipulations en ligne, etc.). Ils estiment que, sur ces questions, ils ont besoin des autres démocraties, tout particulièrement en Europe. Cette situation est inédite et très différente des périodes antérieures où les démocrates américains (la période Clinton, l’époque Obama) pensaient que ce qui était bon pour l’Amérique était, dans une très large mesure, bon pour le reste du monde (« le consensus de Washington »). Aujourd’hui, le représentant démocrate du Maryland Jamie Raskin, qui va prendre la présidence de la commission judiciaire de la Chambre des représentants (House Judiciary Committee) à la place du républicain Jim Jordan, l’une des figures du camp MAGA au Congrès, plaide ainsi pour une conversation entre démocraties sur leurs enjeux communs. Les évolutions politiques en Europe, en particulier en France et en Allemagne, seront également déterminantes pour l’avenir de la relation transatlantique. Les profondes réticences, et même les oppositions de principe à l’approfondissement de l’agenda transatlantique, pourraient cependant venir tout autant des États-Unis, y compris de la part de certaines composantes du parti démocrate, dont les élus sont soumis à des influences contradictoires quant au rapport à l’Europe, en particulier sur les questions de régulation des grandes entreprises numériques. Le contexte n’a pourtant jamais été aussi favorable, pour peu que les Européens comprennent la séquence américaine qui s’ouvre et parviennent à s’y inscrire. Renaud Lassus Les fondateurs ou dirigeants de ces entreprises vont désormais chercher activement à se rapprocher des démocrates après deux ans d’alliance avec Donald Trump. Comme ils l’ont fait auprès de Donald Trump, ils plaideront au Congrès pour une offensive contre la régulation européenne d’Internet et de l’intelligence artificielle. Les réticences de Gavin Newsom, gouverneur sortant de Californie et probable candidat à la prochaine présidentielle, envers le projet de taxation des très grandes fortunes dans son État (qui vient d’être rejeté par référendum le jour même des midterms), ou l’abandon récent par Rob Bonta, procureur général de Californie, d’une procédure antitrust visant le rachat de Warner Bros. par Paramount, au profit d’un accord amiable vivement critiqué par d’autres démocrates, rappellent que l’influence des grands monopoles est un phénomène structurel qui dépasse les clivages partisans aux États-Unis. C’est pourquoi il est d’autant plus essentiel de formuler des propositions, pour ne pas laisser le champ libre aux seuls partisans, des deux côtés de l’Atlantique, d’un agenda d’opposition, voire de confrontation, entre les démocraties européennes et américaine. L’article Après les midterms, une fenêtre pour la relation transatlantique ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: FG records N4.69trn fiscal deficit in Q1’26 as revenue falls
items.description: •Nigeria’s economy grows 3.89% – Budget Office By Udeme Akpan The Federal Government (FG) recorded an aggregate fiscal deficit of N4.69 trillion in the first quarter of 2026, as revenue generation fell significantly below target, highlighting challenges in financing the 2026 budget. This came as Nigeria’s economy grew by 3.89 per cent in real terms during the quarter, driven by improved performance in the oil and non-oil sectors. Figures from the Budget Office of the Federation (BOF), contained in its 2026 Budget Performance Report, showed that the fiscal deficit was N4.69 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N7.86 trillion for the January–March period, representing N3.18 trillion below projection. The report showed that aggregate Federal Government revenue stood at N5.08 trillion, compared with the quarterly target of N9.22 trillion, resulting in a shortfall of N4.14 trillion. This represented about 55 per cent of projected revenue. Similarly, aggregate government expenditure amounted to N9.76 trillion, against the projected N17.08 trillion, indicating an underperformance of N7.32 trillion, or about 57.2 per cent of the target. On deficit financing, domestic borrowing stood at N3.9 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N4.61 trillion, leaving a shortfall of N704.03 billion. However, foreign borrowing, projected at N2.70 trillion for the quarter, recorded no actual inflow during the period. The Federal Government also realised N287.44 billion from multilateral and bilateral project-tied loans, against the quarterly target of N512.23 billion, while privatisation proceeds stood at N3.32 billion, compared with the projected N47.29 billion. The figures highlight the government’s difficulties in generating sufficient revenue and accessing planned financing sources to support budget implementation. Nigeria’s economy grows 3.89% On economic performance, the Budget Office reported that the oil sector grew by 2.57 per cent year-on-year in real terms during the first quarter, up by 0.70 percentage points from 1.87 per cent recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The non-oil sector expanded by 3.94 per cent, outperforming the oil sector and accounting for a larger share of the economy’s growth. The Budget Office described the performance as “a period of macroeconomic stabilisation accompanied by moderate real-sector expansion.” However, it identified weak, although improving, revenue performance as a major constraint to budget execution, noting that the Federal Government continued to meet its non-discretionary expenditure obligations. It stated: “Improving revenue collections in the subsequent quarters of the year is critical to the successful execution of the 2026 Budget.” The report said the government would intensify efforts to improve economic growth and revenue generation, while controlling recurrent expenditure, particularly personnel costs. On strategies to strengthen the economy, the Budget Office identified oil production recovery, tax-base expansion, improved tax compliance, increased domestic production, agricultural productivity, infrastructure development, private-sector credit and export diversification as key priorities. It stated: “The central policy challenge for the remainder of 2026 is therefore not simply to preserve stability, but to convert stability into higher productive capacity and stronger domestic revenue mobilisation.” The report further explained that consolidating gains in inflation management, exchange-rate stability and the external sector would require creating sufficient room for productive private-sector credit, investment and employment generation. It added that controlling recurrent expenditure, particularly personnel costs, and addressing security challenges remained important to improving fiscal performance. On budget implementation, the Budget Office reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to transparency and accountability, stating that it would ensure “firm adherence to budget implementation guidelines and the governance framework on monitoring of capital budget implementation.” It added that efforts would focus on improving budget execution efficiency and ensuring effective project management in the remaining quarters of 2026. items.title: Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar
items.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Police Command on Wednesday arrested a 27-year-old man, Victor Edet Yellow Duke, in connection with an attack on the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, in Calabar, the state capital. The attack left the windshields of some vehicles smashed. The incident occurred at about 2:20 p.m. at the Watt Market Roundabout as the convoy was returning from the palace of the Obong of Calabar to Metropolitan Hotel, the venue of the party’s presidential town hall meeting. According to the police, a group of suspected hoodlums, reportedly armed with machetes and sticks, emerged from the Calabar Road and Clerks Alley axis and attacked vehicles in the convoy. The number of vehicles affected had not been ascertained. Police personnel deployed in the area moved in swiftly to contain the situation. Their intervention, which included the use of tear gas, led to the arrest of the suspect, while the other attackers fled. The suspect was later taken to the State Police Headquarters by operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, VCRU, for what the command described as a discreet investigation, to prevent reprisals or a further breakdown of law and order. Normalcy has since returned to the area. In a statement by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, the command said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, had ordered a thorough investigation to identify and arrest other participants and establish the full circumstances of the incident. Cautioning against presuming the suspect’s guilt, the police said: “The arrest of a suspect does not amount to a determination of guilt, as the suspect remains entitled to the presumption of innocence pending the conclusion of investigation and any subsequent judicial proceedings.” The command assured residents, political stakeholders and visitors that adequate security measures remained in place across the state. It reiterated its commitment to “providing equal security protection to all political parties, candidates and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation.” It also urged the public to stay calm, avoid spreading unverified information and report suspicious activities through established police channels. Eitokpah added: “The Cross River State Police Command remains committed to maintaining public safety, protecting democratic participation and ensuring that all lawful political activities are conducted in a peaceful and secure environment.” The post Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: US Midterms: Implications of democrats’ victory
items.description: PRESIDENT Donald Trump has acknowledged the impact of the United States’ attack on Iran and a sharp rise in gasoline prices on stunning Republican losses in midterm elections, but said the move was justified and denied responsibility for the rout. The Democrats won both the US Senate and House of Representatives, taking control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump’s presidency. The tally showed that Democrats grabbed 54 and 234 seats at press time to win the Senate and House of Representatives respectively. Historic firsts The election also delivered some historic firsts with the Democrats flipping at least seven Senate seats in ruby-red states and battlegrounds like Kansas, which hasn’t elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. They held on to battleground seats in Georgia and Michigan. In the the House, Democrats would start the year with what would be its largest majority in nearly two decades, NBC News projects. Democrats flipped more than two dozen districts, some that voted for Trump by double digits in 2024. In the gubernatorial races, Democrats also flipped GOP-held offices: Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia, Amy Acton in Ohio, Rob Sand in Iowa, Gina Hinojosa in Texas and Aaron Ford in Nevada. Specifically, David Crowley, Democrat, has become the first Black governor in U.S history, Abdul El-Sayed becomes the first Muslim ever elected to the U.S. Senate, James Talarico becomes the first Democrat elected in Texas since 1988, Xavier Becerra becomes the first Latino elected governor in California history, Gina Hinojosa becomes the first Latina elected governor in Texas history, while Deb Haaland becomes the first Native American woman elected governor in U.S. History. I’m willing to accept results, work with Democrats – Trump Reacting to the election defeat, Trump said he was willing to accept the results of the midterm elections and work with Democrats as they made gains across the country. “We’ll, you know, look forward to working with them,” he told The New York Times shortly before 10:30 p.m. while watching results come in. “We’ll probably work something out.” Trump said Democrats had reached out to him about working together and that he thought they could find common ground on the debt ceiling. He added that he has “total veto power, so they have to come to us.” In a preview of his likely governing style over the next two years, Trump also posted a picture of his trademark red cap emblazoned with the word “veto” to convey his determination to block legislation carried by the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress. Iran war impact Blaming Iran war, Trump said: “We actually have the greatest economy, but because of the gasoline price, people don’t see it as much as they would have without it. And the gasoline was caused by Iran,” he told Fox News in a televised phone interview late on Tuesday. “People agree with what I’m doing on Iran, but they really probably weren’t willing to do the short-term consequence of paying more for gasoline. I understand that. I don’t agree with it.” Speaking to The Wall Street Journal about the Republican defeats, Trump said about the Iran war: “I did the right thing. I would have done it again.” Vance also fingers Iran war Vice President JD Vance, a likely 2028 presidential candidate and heir apparent to Trump’s Make America Great Again movement, appeared to diverge from Trump’s thinking on the wisdom of the conflict. “The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night,” he wrote. “If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so.” “Everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.” Republican strategist, James Davis, said the war contributed to the setbacks for the party but also to a lack of clear messaging. “The war was definitely part of it and has helped shift the electorate toward Democrats. But the biggest issue was not the war itself, but the clear articulation of a strategy that gives people confidence in that strategy,” Davis told Al Jazeera. The economic fallout from the conflict, including higher energy and especially diesel costs, had affected all sectors of the economy and intensified Americans’ concerns about affordability, he added. Blaming candidates Democratic leader vows to end Iran war, investigate Trump Meanwhile, Senate Democratic leader, Chuck Schumer, has vowed that the Democrats will end the war in Iran through the “power of the purse” next year when they take control of the Senate. “We are going to end the war. We’ve got some Republicans who have joined us in ending the war and the Founding Fathers had the power of the purse as one of the ways of deterring a president who does war without the consent of the American people,” Schumer said at a Capitol Hill news conference, a day after Democrats won the majority in the chamber. “The American people don’t know the heck we are fighting for in Iran. He’s never made it clear; he changes his mind day to day and minute to minute, ” he added. Schumer said the election, in which Democrats currently have a 54-44 edge over Republicans with two seats not called, created a “generational remake of the Senate.” But he acknowledged Democrats will have to prove to voters they will address their concerns about high prices and corruption. “Many of the folks who voted for us are skeptical,” he said. What loss means for Trump’s remaining 2 years With the massive loss, Trump could face impeachment threats as the House also has the power to impeach a president – the first step of Congress’ process to remove an official from office. The Republican Party would be looking nervously towards the 2028 election. For the first time since 2016, there is likely to be a serious debate within the party about whether to move on from the aggressive nationalism and Trump’s “Make America Great Again” movement. Democrats, meanwhile, face their own questions about how to capitalise on their victories. Besides, Committees in both the US Senate and House have investigative powers, which they could use to delve into alleged conflicts of interest and other actions by the president and those close to him. The Senate also has the power to confirm or block the president’s cabinet and judicial nominations. Foreign policy futures But for the rest of the world, change might not come so quickly. Despite the fact that his party has suffered this electoral setback, Trump remains president until 2028. And because despite its constitutional role in declaring war and ratifying treaties, Congress tends to be less involved in foreign policy, there is still a lot that he can do with that power. Indeed, US presidents whose parties perform badly in midterm elections often become more active in foreign policy than they had previously. With the chance of passing a significant domestic agenda mostly beyond their reach, they have more time on their hands to think about America’s relations with the rest of the world. The same is likely to be true of Trump. The fact that the midterms are over also means that Trump no longer has to be so careful about the political consequences of his actions. As the midterm elections got closer, the president has backed down from major military confrontation with Iran and sought a truce in his tariff wars. Now, with political constraints lifted, he could become more erratic and unpredictable. Vanguard News The post US Midterms: Implications of democrats’ victory appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Agalga plans visit to detained Kwame Frimpong amid extradition proceedings
items.description: Majority Leader James Agalga plans to visit detained Asante Akyem North MP Ohene Kwame Frimpong to get firsthand information about his case as extradition proceedings continue in the Netherlands. Speaking on JoyNews’ PM Express on Wednesday, Mr Agalga said he would make the trip when his parliamentary workload eases. “I do not know the actual details. In fact, when the pressures of work ease a bit, I intend to pay him a visit.” He said the visit would help him understand the circumstances surrounding his colleague’s detention. “To obtain firsthand information about what is happening,” he explained. Mr Agalga confirmed that he had been formally briefed on the matter. He expressed hope that the applications before the Dutch court would succeed. “We pray for our colleague that the applications that are currently before the court would come out favourably for him.” Mr Frimpong was arrested at Amsterdam’s Schiphol Airport on May 10, 2026, following a US extradition request. The case concerns allegations of romance scams and money laundering. He has not been convicted. Two attempts to secure bail have failed. His substantive extradition hearing is scheduled for November 18, according to Majority Chief Whip Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor. He has also dismissed reports that the MP has already been transferred to the United States. Following the arrest, Parliament engaged Ghana’s diplomatic mission in The Hague. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa also confirmed consular assistance, including a visit to the detained MP. In Wednesday’s interview, Mr Agalga said Ghana’s mission in Brussels had been supportive. He welcomed that assistance and stressed that Parliament must uphold the presumption of innocence. “So we wish our colleague well. He’s innocent until proven guilty. Then there’s unanimity in Parliament that we must respect that principle.” He also rejected suggestions that Parliament should declare Mr Frimpong’s seat vacant because of his detention. “No, we can’t do that. He’s not been convicted. If you declare the seat vacant and the courts clear him, what happens?” Mr Agalga said Parliament had to respect the detained MP’s rights. “To do otherwise would amount to a violation of his rights.”

items.title: Kwakye Ofosu cuts sod for construction of new classrooms in AAK
items.description: Felix Kwakye Ofosu, the Member of Parliament (MP) for the Abura-Asebu-Kwamankese (AAK) Constituency, has initiated steps to address the persistent challenge of inadequate classroom infrastructure in some communities within the constituency. A sod-cutting ceremony for the construction of several classroom blocks has therefore been held at Abura Dunkwa. When completed, the classrooms would improve access to quality education and provide a more conducive teaching and learning environment, eliminating schools under trees and other unsuitable structures in Abura Dunkwa and its adjoining communities. The MP, together with Mr Daniel Mensah Wardy, the District Chief Executive (DCE) for AAK, jointly performed the ceremony to commence the construction of a three-unit classroom block, office and a store with ancillary facilities at Obenkrom, and a two-unit classroom block with the same facilities at Kwesi Amaa. The Moree community, also in the AAK Constituency, is also to expect phase two of an ultramodern 12-unit classroom block with ancillary facilities and a two-unit classroom block with an office space, a store and ancillary facilities also earmarked for construction at Korado. They also broke ground for Community Health Planning and Services Compounds at New Ebu and Katakyiase with an accommodation and a mechanised borehole projects and inspected a completed Free Primary Healthcare Post at Moree. Mr Kwakye Ofosu, addressing the media after the tour, admitted that the constituency also had schools under trees which were being replaced with modern infrastructure. He further underscored the importance of education as a critical driver of human development and national progress and indicated that addressing the infrastructural challenges of basic schools remained essential to ensuring that children in rural communities within AAK were not disadvantaged in their pursuit of education. Classroom blocks to be completed within the next six months would be handed over to bring relief to beneficiary schools and help end the ‘Schools Under Trees’ phenomenon in AAK, the MP added.

items.title: 2027 Budget must prioritise tourism development – Consultant
items.description: Emmanuel Frimpong, a tourism consultant, has urged the government to prioritise funding and implementation of tourism, arts and culture projects in the 2027 Budget to drive investment, create jobs and boost economic growth. He said effective implementation of existing policy commitments would strengthen businesses and improve livelihoods. In an interview with the Ghana News Agency in Accra on Wednesday, Mr Frimpong, who is also the founder of the Africa Tourism Research Network, said the Budget should prioritise tourism infrastructure, sustainable financing for the creative industry and regional tourism development. He called for increased and timely funding to rehabilitate heritage sites, develop community-based tourism, improve access roads to tourist attractions and complete abandoned or stalled projects. Mr Frimpong also urged the government to operationalise and sustain the Creative Arts Fund and Film Development Fund to provide musicians, filmmakers, event organisers and other creative entrepreneurs with predictable financing. “The creative industry needs predictable financing, not just periodic announcements,” he said. Mr Frimpong said improved infrastructure, streamlined regulatory processes and stronger public-private partnerships would help attract domestic and international investors. He also identified tourism education, skills development and professional training as priorities, saying infrastructure alone could not make destinations competitive without a skilled workforce capable of delivering services that met international standards. On regional tourism, he called for support for emerging destinations and local tourism enterprises across all 16 regions to address the concentration of investment and visitor activities in a few established centres. He said expanding investment beyond major tourism destinations would create opportunities for local businesses and enable more communities to benefit from the country’s tourism resources. Mr Frimpong called for stronger tourism data systems, including a Tourism Satellite Account, to measure the sector’s contribution to Gross Domestic Product, employment and national revenue. He said the Budget should include clear performance indicators, implementation timelines and accountability mechanisms to track government interventions and assess their impact. Mr Frimpong said the sector’s performance should be measured not only by visitor numbers but also by income retained in local communities, sustainable jobs created and the commercial viability of tourism businesses. “My key expectation is that the 2027 Budget should move Ghana’s tourism, arts and culture sector from policy commitments to measurable economic outcomes,” he said. He said collaboration among the government, private sector operators, local authorities and communities was essential to sustainable growth in the sector.

items.title: 2026 tourism budget implementation promising, but incomplete – Analyst
items.description: Emmanuel Frimpong, a Tourism Consultant and Analyst, says Ghana’s implementation of tourism, arts and culture initiatives outlined in the 2026 Budget has been promising but remains incomplete. He said although progress had been made in institutional development, digitalisation and cultural promotion, several major commitments were still at the preparatory or implementation stages, and urged the Government to shift its focus from policy announcements to measurable results. He cited the introduction of the Ghana Tourism Marketplace and the Ghana Tourism Investment Platform as important developments aimed at improving market access for tourism businesses and connecting investors to opportunities in the sector. He also highlighted initiatives such as AfroGastro, the promotion of Ghanaian cuisine in hospitality establishments, and renovation works and facility upgrades at the National Theatre. In an interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA) in Accra on Wednesday, Mr Frimpong said the establishment of digital platforms and the release of funds were commendable, but the industry needed corresponding improvements in infrastructure, access to financing, business growth, and sustainable job creation. He explained that the Ghana Tourism Marketplace gave tourism businesses opportunities to showcase and sell their products and experiences, while the investment platform could connect potential investors with hotels, tourist attractions, and community-based tourism enterprises. However, he said the interventions’ benefits were not yet evenly distributed, particularly among small tourism businesses operating outside the country’s major tourism centres. He identified poor access roads, inadequate financing, limited digital skills, weak marketing capacity, and insufficient visitor facilities as challenges confronting operators. Mr Frimpong said digital tourism promotion must go hand in hand with physical infrastructure development, noting that although tourists could discover destinations online, the quality of roads, sanitation, security, accommodation and visitor services would ultimately determine their experience. On the sector’s economic performance, he said Ghana recorded 1,306,962 international tourist arrivals in 2025, generating an estimated US$4.34 billion in revenue. Domestic tourism visits also increased from 1.68 million in 2024 to 1.79 million in 2025, while licensed tourism enterprises grew by 6.1 per cent and travel trade enterprises by 18.6 per cent. He cautioned, however, against attributing those figures directly to the implementation of the 2026 Budget, since they largely reflected the sector’s performance in 2025. Mr Frimpong said the Government needed to provide more detailed information on jobs created through individual projects, businesses benefiting from interventions, funds disbursed, private investments attracted and revenue generated. He called for the timely release and use of approved budgetary allocations, completion of outstanding infrastructure projects, improved tourism data systems, and accessible financing for small and medium-sized enterprises in the tourism and creative industries. He also advocated establishing a Tourism Satellite Account (TSA) to provide more accurate information on tourism’s contribution to Gross Domestic Product, employment and national revenue. Mr Frimpong said stronger collaboration among the Government, private sector operators, local authorities and communities was necessary to ensure that tourism growth translated into improved livelihoods. He said the industry’s success should be measured not only by visitor numbers but also by the income retained in local communities, sustainable jobs created and the commercial viability of tourism businesses.

items.title: Africa urged to unite on digital governance agenda
items.description: African countries must forge a common digital governance agenda to bridge the digital divide and safeguard the continent’s future, Vice President Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has said. She said decisions on digital technologies would have far-reaching implications for commerce, education and individual freedoms across Africa. Speaking on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama at the opening of the 15th Africa Internet Governance Forum (AfIGF 2026) in Accra, Professor Opoku-Agyemang called for a united African approach to advancing digital inclusion, innovation and trust. The forum, held under the theme, “Advancing Africa’s Digital Future Through Innovation, Inclusion and Trust,” brought together governments, technology experts, civil society organisations and young people to discuss internet governance and digital policy. The Vice President said Ghana was implementing measures to narrow the digital divide, including the distribution of digital devices to universities and the development of a National Artificial Intelligence Strategy. “Closing the digital divide involves more than extending network coverage. It also requires attention to affordability, accessibility, and the skills people need to use digital technologies,” she stated. Prof. Opoku-Agyemang said the safety, privacy and educational rights of children and young people must remain central to digital policy. Mr Samuel Nartey George, Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, called for Africa to take ownership of its digital future. He said Africa must determine how it governs its digital space and shapes technological development to serve its interests. Quoting Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, the Minister stated: “We face neither east nor west, we face forward.” Mr George said Africa must develop digital solutions that reflected its realities rather than rely on imported models. He identified priorities including connectivity, affordable devices, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, data protection, child online safety and national language models for artificial intelligence. “Unity does not mean conformity. Every country will chart its own path, but we can agree on common goals, common standards, and a common voice,” he said. The Minister said Ghana was ready to serve as Chair of the African Union Specialised Technical Committee on Communications and ICT from 2026 to 2028. The forum forms part of continental preparations for global discussions on internet governance and coincides with the 20-year review of the World Summit on the Information Society and the Global Digital Compact.

items.title: LZB, ERTMS y CDI 113 + 200: una semana descifrando los 17 minutos del accidente de Urda
items.description: A las 6.30 del miércoles 28 de octubre, un trabajador del centro de control de Adif en Atocha (Madrid) empieza su turno con una reunión de media hora en la que se le informa de cómo marchan las operaciones de alta velocidad hasta ese momento. Poco más de dos horas después, el sistema de seguridad LZB , que impide que dos trenes coincidan en el mismo punto, se cae en un tramo de más de 63 kilómetros en la vía de altas prestaciones que une Madrid con Sevilla. Siete trenes se paralizan inmediatamente. Son las 8.30. Ese trabajador de Adif ordena seis minutos después que el AVE 2080 reemprenda la circulación a marcha normal, pese a que el protocolo de aplicación en esa situación especifica que debe ir a una velocidad lo suficientemente lenta (marcha a la vista) como para detenerse si aparece un obstáculo en la vía. Apenas 17 minutos después , ese convoy, lanzado a entre 160 y 200 kilómetros por hora, se empotra contra un Iryo completamente detenido a las puertas de la estación de Urda (Toledo), provocando al menos 69 muertos y cientos de heridos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Dirigentes del PSOE se aferran a la “lección política” de Puente y la derrota de Trump para relanzar la campaña
items.description: El ánimo del PSOE vuelve a levantarse. La dimisión de Óscar Puente, tan inesperada como oportuna para muchos socialistas, ha tenido un efecto balsámico instantáneo a poco más de tres semanas del 29-N. Los mismos pesos pesados de Ferraz y La Moncloa que hace una semana daban por perdidas las generales tras el accidente ferroviario de Urda han recobrado el optimismo con la asunción de responsabilidades de Puente “por dignidad” y “estar a la altura” de España que, según interpretan todos los dirigentes socialistas consultados, les permite diferenciarse de la reacción del PP en otras catástrofes. “Óscar ha dado una lección política de primer nivel. No todos somos iguales”, resume un presidente autonómico. La derrota por aplastamiento de Donald Trump en las elecciones de mitad de mandato de Estados Unidos, con victorias impensables hace unos días en bastiones republicanos como Texas, Kansas o Iowa, también ha contribuido a devolver la esperanza en otra remontada imposible como la de 2023. “Ocurrió en Brasil, acaba de ocurrir en Estados Unidos y ocurrirá pronto en España. La ola ultra a la que pretenden subirse Feijóo y Abascal ya no crece: se desmorona”, fue el diagnóstico de Pedro Sánchez. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Bernardo Arévalo, presidente de Guatemala: “Tenemos que oponernos a la normalización del autoritarismo y las dictaduras”
items.description: Bernardo Arévalo (Montevideo, 68 años) ha tenido que remar a contracorriente desde que asumió el Gobierno de Guatemala en enero de 2024. Tras denunciar intentos de golpe de Estado para impedir su llegada al poder, el mandatario ha debido lidiar con el desgaste político, gobernar con una minoría en el Congreso, afrontar la suspensión y fragmentación de su partido y luchar para llevar a buen puerto una serie de nombramientos en instancias clave del Estado, como la Fiscalía General y el Tribunal Supremo Electoral. A todo eso se suman las turbulencias, las presiones y las responsabilidades propias del cargo. “Es complicado, pero no imposible”, afirma Arévalo sobre su día a día en la silla presidencial. De visita en Madrid en el marco de la XXX Cumbre Iberoamericana , el único presidente progresista de Centroamérica analiza en una entrevista con EL PAÍS la actualidad política de la región y hace balance a poco más de un año de concluir su mandato. Seguir leyendo

items.description: La dimisión de Óscar Puente actúa como fusible. Es difícil imaginar que la salida del exministro de Transportes se hubiera producido si no hubiera elecciones el 29 de noviembre. Ello no quita que la asunción de responsabilidades políticas fuera obligatoria ante una setentena de víctimas mortales. Y aun así, el Pedro Sánchez más implacable con sus fieles colaboradores se hace notar ante las urnas: hasta la exportavoz nacional del PSOE, Montse Mínguez, dimitió porque su pareja alquilaba pisos.
